stem: Which of the following uses an organic compound that emits light?
explanation: Organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displays use an organic compound or film that emits light. Each OLED pixel makes its own light, so the panel needs no backlight.
whyWrong: Mini-LED is an LCD backlight made of many small LEDs; it uses no organic compound and resists burn-in better than OLED.
IPS is an LCD panel technology that widens the viewing angle; the liquid crystals do not emit light themselves.
An LCD needs a separate backlight because its liquid crystals only block or pass light.
An LED display uses ordinary light-emitting diodes, usually as a backlight, not an organic film.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which of the following are possible reasons a laptop’s LCD suddenly went blank with no user intervention? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: A damaged inverter or a burned-out backlight bulb can make a laptop's display go blank. You can check whether the LCD still gets a signal by shining a flashlight at the screen: a faint image means the panel works but has no light.
whyWrong: A damaged LCD usually still works partly, with cracks, missing areas, or other visible damage, instead of going fully blank.
A wrong resolution setting can blank or garble the screen, but only after someone changes it, and the user made no change.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which term refers to pixel density?
explanation: PPI (pixels per inch) measures the pixel density of a display. A higher PPI packs more pixels into each inch, so the image looks sharper at the same screen size.
whyWrong: Hz measures the refresh rate, which is how many times per second the display redraws the screen.
SDR (standard dynamic range) describes the normal brightness and color range of a display, not its pixel density.
FPS (frames per second) is how many frames the video source draws each second, not a property of the screen's pixels.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 12: Device Display Components, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: You are a technician for a small organization of 50 employees. You are tasked with replacing a damaged LED screen on a mobile computer. After installing a new LED screen, you find that the OS can be seen on the screen, but the touchscreen is not working. Which of the following are the MOST LIKELY root causes of this failure? (Select the three best answers.)
options: The touchscreen needs to be calibrated after replacement.
The hardware replacement in the scenario is not touchscreen capable.
A grounding screw is not attached securely.
The digitizer cable is not attached to the motherboard properly.
The LCD panel firmware should be updated.
explanation: The touchscreen drivers might need to be installed, the replacement panel might not be touchscreen capable, or the digitizer cable might not be attached to the motherboard properly. Always install drivers, buy the exact model of screen, and check that cables are secure before closing the system.
whyWrong: Calibration fixes a touchscreen whose touch position is off, not one that does not respond at all.
A loose grounding screw would not disable only the touchscreen while the display works.
Panel firmware is normally set by the manufacturer and does not need updating after a screen replacement.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 33

stem: Which of the following monitor types provide for the widest viewing angle, along with rich colors and consistent backlighting? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: IPS (in-plane switching) technology offers the widest viewing angle of the LCD panel types. LED-backlit monitors give rich colors and consistent backlighting and also work well in areas with a lot of natural light.
whyWrong: VA (vertical alignment) screens are much better than TN screens but have a narrower viewing angle than IPS.
TN (twisted nematic) monitors are inexpensive but have the narrowest viewing angle of the three panel types.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 45

stem: You are installing a replacement monitor on a desktop computer. Which of the following is true regarding a monitor's refresh rate?
options: As long as the graphics adapter can refresh the image at a particular rate, the attached monitor can accommodate that refresh rate.
The refresh rate is normally expressed in MHz.
The refresh rate is normally selected by using the controls on the front panel of the monitor.
As you lower the resolution, the maximum refresh rate allowed tends to increase.
explanation: As you lower the resolution, the maximum refresh rate allowed tends to increase. Both the monitor and the adapter must support a refresh rate before it can be used.
whyWrong: Both the monitor and the adapter must support a refresh rate; if either does not, the rate cannot be used.
The refresh rate is expressed in hertz (Hz), not millions of cycles per second (MHz).
The refresh rate is usually selected in the operating system's display settings, not in the monitor's menu.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 4

stem: Your manager tells you to replace the inverter on a broken laptop. Where will you find this component?
options: Next to the heat sink and fan
explanation: The inverter, which transforms DC power into AC power for an LCD backlight, is found in the display. It sits near the backlight it powers, in the lid of the laptop.
whyWrong: The area underneath the keyboard is in the bottom half of the laptop, not in the display.
The heat sink and fan are in the bottom half of the laptop, away from the display.
The CPU is in the bottom half of the laptop, while the inverter is in the display.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 2

stem: You need to replace an LCD on a defective laptop. Which of the following are components of an LCD? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: The components of an LCD screen are the inverter, screen, and backlight. LCD display units will also have a Wi-Fi antenna (not the card), webcam, and microphone.
whyWrong: The Wi-Fi card sits in the base of the laptop; only its antenna runs through the display.
There is no LCD component called a backdrop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of the following describes the job of an inverter in a laptop?
options: It changes the screen orientation when the laptop is rotated.
It converts AC power into DC power for the display backlight.
It converts DC power into AC power for the display backlight.
It allows the laptop display to function in tablet mode.
explanation: The laptop power supply converts AC power into DC power for the laptop's internal circuitry. The display backlight, if used, needs AC power. The inverter's job is to convert (invert) the DC power into AC power for the backlight.
whyWrong: Screen rotation is handled by an accelerometer and the OS, not by the inverter.
The conversion runs the other way: the inverter turns DC into AC for the backlight.
Tablet mode is a function of the 2-in-1 hinge and OS, not of the inverter.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 10

stem: A user on your network wants to be able to draw images on a screen and have the laptop capture them. What type of device needs to be installed on their laptop?
explanation: The user needs a digitizer, which takes input from the device, such as drawn images, and converts them into electronic images on the computer. The user could also use a touchscreen for the same purpose.
whyWrong: An inverter changes DC power into AC power for a display backlight.
There is no laptop device called a capturer.
A trackpad is a pointing device that controls the mouse cursor, not a drawing surface that captures images.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 4: Laptop and Mobile Device Hardware, Review Questions question 12

stem: What do we call the time it takes for all of the sub-pixels on the panel to change from one state to another?
explanation: The time it takes for all of the sub-pixels on the panel to go from pure black to pure white and back again is called the response rate. A lower response rate, measured in milliseconds, means less blurring or ghosting in fast-moving images.
whyWrong: Refresh rate is how many times per second the display redraws the whole screen, not how fast a sub-pixel changes state.
Redraw rate is not a standard display specification.
Transfer rate describes how fast data moves across a bus or drive interface, not a panel attribute.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 1
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 17: response rate is not listed under the 3.1 attributes; closest topic is Attributes (refresh rates).

stem: What provides the illumination for LCD monitors?
explanation: The backlights provide the illumination for the LCD panel. The liquid crystals only block or pass light, so an LCD needs a CCFL or LED backlight behind the panel to produce a visible image.
whyWrong: The inverter only converts DC to AC to power a CCFL backlight; it does not produce the light itself.
A lamp is the light source of a projector, not of an LCD monitor.
The LCD panel shapes the image but emits no light of its own.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 2

stem: How do you measure brightness of a projector?
explanation: The brightness of a projector is measured in lumens. A higher lumen rating lets a projector give a clear image in a room with more ambient light.
whyWrong: Pixels describe the resolution of the image, not its brightness.
LEDs are one kind of light source a projector can use, not a unit of measure.
CCFLs are fluorescent backlights used in older LCD panels, not a measure of brightness.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 4
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 17: projectors are not listed under 3.1; closest topic is display Attributes.

stem: Which of these aspect ratios is associated with ultrawide monitors?
explanation: The widest aspect ratio among this group, 21:9, is associated with ultrawide monitors. Most standard widescreen monitors use 16:9.
whyWrong: 16:9 is the standard widescreen ratio of most monitors and TVs, not ultrawide.
4:3 is the nearly square ratio of older monitors.
3:2 is a taller ratio used on some laptops and tablets, not an ultrawide one.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 5
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 17: aspect ratio is not listed by name; closest is Attributes (screen resolution).

stem: Which of these is not a light-emitting technology?
explanation: Because it does not emit its own light, liquid crystal display (LCD) technology requires a backlight. CCFL and LED backlights produce light, and each OLED pixel emits its own light.
whyWrong: A CCFL is a fluorescent lamp that emits light as an LCD backlight.
LEDs emit light and are the most common backlight in modern LCD panels.
Each OLED pixel emits its own light, so OLED panels need no backlight.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 8

stem: Projectors with which of the following kinds of light source take longer to start up and shut down?
explanation: Projector lamps need time to heat up before the projector is ready and time to cool down after use. LED and laser light sources turn on and off almost at once.
whyWrong: CCFLs are backlights for LCD panels, not a common projector light source.
Laser light sources reach full brightness almost instantly.
LED light sources start up and shut down quickly with no warm-up time.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 10
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 17: projector light sources are not listed under 3.1; closest topic is Types. Related: 5.3 Burnt-out bulb.

stem: What is a type of sensing device that detects the locations and duration of contact across its face, usually by a finger or stylus?
explanation: A touchscreen is a type of sensing device that detects the locations and duration of contact across its face, usually by a finger or stylus. The digitizer layer turns those touches into input the device can use.
whyWrong: A trackpad senses finger movement but is not a display.
A touchpad senses finger movement to move the pointer but is not part of the screen.
A laptop is a type of computer, not a sensing device.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Which of the following display types will you commonly find on a laptop today?
explanation: You will see only LCD displays on portables today, though they may be marketed as LED displays because of their LED backlights. OLED screens also appear on some newer laptops.
whyWrong: CRT monitors are far too large and heavy for a laptop.
A CCFL is an older backlight for LCD panels, not a display type.
Plasma displays were used in large TVs, not laptops.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 23: Portable Computing, Chapter Review question 6
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 23: the book predates common OLED laptops; LCD is still the most common laptop display.

stem: Which of the following is used in mobile devices to convert analog video and sound to digital video and sound?
explanation: Digitizers are used in mobile devices to convert analog signals to digital ones, such as the analog signals of touch movement on a screen. The digitizer layer of a touch screen turns each touch into digital input the device can use.
whyWrong: Calibration adjusts how touches line up with the screen; a calibrator does not convert signals.
An SDK is a software development kit for writing apps.
A virtual assistant is voice-controlled software, not a conversion component.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 24: Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 1

stem: John has a high-resolution image on his iPad of his two-year-old son and the family dog. The image initially displays smaller than the screen, so he wants to zoom in to get the details of his son’s expression. What gesture can he use to accomplish this task?
options: Click the mouse in the middle of the picture to select it, then use the scroll wheel on the mouse to zoom in.
Tap the picture with his index finger on his son’s face.
Long-press on the image and select zoom from the pop-up menu.
Touch his son’s face on the screen with his thumb and finger, then pinch outward to zoom in.
explanation: John should touch his son's face on the screen with his thumb and finger, then pinch outward to zoom in. A multitouch screen detects both fingers and enlarges the image around them.
whyWrong: An iPad is used with touch, and this method is not the touch gesture for zooming.
A single tap selects or opens an item; it does not zoom in.
A long press opens a context menu, which does not offer a zoom option.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 24: Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 2
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 24: gestures are not listed in the current objectives; closest topic is Touch screen/digitizer. Option text 'scroll in' fixed to 'zoom in'.

stem: Which mobile device screen technology uses no backlight?
explanation: OLED technology does not use a backlight. Each organic LED pixel produces its own light.
whyWrong: BYOD is a policy for personal devices at work, not a screen technology.
An LCD screen needs a backlight because its crystals emit no light.
LED-labeled screens are LCDs with an LED backlight.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 24: Mobile Devices, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which of the following describes the function of a digitizer?
options: It converts DC power to AC power
It can support a contrast ratio of 2000:1
It controls the brightness setting on an LCD monitor
It is a piece of glass that is installed on a mobile device to enable the touchscreen to function
explanation: The digitizer is a layer of glass on a mobile device that turns touches into digital signals. It is what makes the touchscreen work.
whyWrong: Converting DC power to AC power is the job of an inverter.
A contrast ratio of 2000:1 is a property of display panels such as VA, not the job of a digitizer.
LCD brightness comes from the backlight and its settings, not the digitizer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 1
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2 (mobile display components); current 3.1.

stem: What is the purpose of an inverter?
options: To convert AC to DC power
To convert DC to AC power
To increase readability in low-light conditions
explanation: An inverter converts DC power to AC power. Older LCD screens with CCFL backlights use an inverter to power the backlight.
whyWrong: Converting AC to DC power is the job of a power supply or AC adapter, not an inverter.
Touchscreen functionality comes from the digitizer.
Readability in low light comes from the backlight.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 4
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; current 3.1 inverter.

stem: When using a high frame rate, the crystals twist or untwist giving the screen a quick response time that helps reduce ghosting and motion trail. Which of the following options is being described?
explanation: Twisted nematic (TN) displays use crystals that twist or untwist depending on the voltage. They have a very fast response time, which reduces ghosting and motion trails at high frame rates.
whyWrong: IPS displays use crystals that rotate rather than twist and are known for color accuracy and wide viewing angles.
VA panels use crystals that tilt, and they are more prone to blurring and ghosting.
A CRT is a legacy display that uses an electron beam and phosphors, not liquid crystals.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 5
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; current 3.1 display types.

stem: Which of the following displays is BEST for both gaming and graphic design?
explanation: In-plane switching (IPS) uses crystals that rotate rather than twist. It gives better color accuracy and wider viewing angles, with response times that are now good enough for gaming. This makes it suitable for both gaming and graphic design.
whyWrong: LED is a type of backlight for LCD panels, and the panel type, not the backlight, decides color accuracy.
LCD is a general family that includes TN, IPS, and VA panels, so it does not name the best panel type.
A CRT is a legacy display that is not suitable for modern gaming or graphic design.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 9
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; current 3.1 display types.

stem: Which of the following displays is prone to ghosting and can support a contrast ratio of 2000:1?
explanation: Vertical alignment (VA) panels use crystals that tilt rather than twist or rotate. They have a high contrast ratio, such as 2000:1 or 3000:1, but slower response times, so they are more prone to blurring and ghosting than TN or IPS panels.
whyWrong: OLED has a near-infinite contrast ratio because each pixel makes its own light, and it has a very fast response time.
IPS panels usually have a lower contrast ratio, about 1000:1 to 1200:1, and are known for color accuracy.
LED describes the backlight of an LCD panel, not the panel type that causes ghosting.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 10
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; current 3.1 display types.

stem: What type of screen is used by monitors, tablets, smartphones, and TV screens and does not use a backlight?
explanation: In an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display, each pixel produces its own light, so the screen needs no separate backlight. OLED is used in modern TVs, smartphones, monitors, and tablets.
whyWrong: A CRT makes light with an electron beam and phosphors, but it is a bulky legacy display that tablets and smartphones do not use.
An LCD needs a backlight because the liquid crystals do not produce light.
An LED display is an LCD panel lit by an LED backlight.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.2 question 11
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.2; current 3.1 display types.

stem: Which of the following uses a 7-pin data connector and a 15-pin power connector?
explanation: SATA connections use a 7-pin data connector and a 15-pin power connector. The data cable carries the signal between the drive and the motherboard, and the power cable comes from the power supply.
whyWrong: VGA is a 15-pin analog video connector, not a drive connection.
An older IDE (PATA) drive uses a 40-pin data cable and a 4-pin Molex power connector.
Molex is a 4-pin power connector for older drives and fans; it has no data connector.
Cat 6 is a twisted pair network cable with eight wires that ends in RJ45 connectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which type of cable would you use if you were concerned about EMI?
explanation: Shielded twisted pair (STP) is the only cable listed here that is built to reduce electromagnetic interference (EMI). Fiber optic cable is another good solution because it carries light, but it costs more and is harder to install.
whyWrong: Plenum-rated cable meets fire code: it burns slowly and gives off fewer toxic fumes, but its jacket gives no EMI shielding.
Unshielded twisted pair has no shield, so it is the most likely of these cables to pick up EMI.
Coaxial cable carries cable TV and cable Internet signals and is not the usual choice for an EMI-resistant LAN run.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: You have been tasked with connecting a newer Android smartphone to an external TV so that you can display the CEO’s smartphone screen during a meeting. Which of the following adapters would typically be the BEST solution?
explanation: Typically, you would use a USB-C to HDMI adapter. A newer Android smartphone most likely has a USB-C port, and HDMI is the most likely input on a TV.
whyWrong: Newer Android smartphones have moved from Micro-USB to USB-C, so this adapter would probably not fit the phone.
Newer phones use USB-C instead of Micro-USB, and TVs normally do not have DVI inputs.
TVs normally do not have DVI inputs, so this adapter would not connect to the TV.
A USB-C to Ethernet adapter connects a device to a wired network, not to a display.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which type of cable can connect a computer to another computer directly?
explanation: A crossover cable connects like devices directly: computer to computer, or switch to switch. It uses the T568A wiring standard on one end and T568B on the other end.
whyWrong: A straight-through (patch) cable connects different devices, for example a computer to a switch.
T568A is a wiring standard for the pin order in a connector, not a type of cable on its own.
SATA cables connect storage drives inside a computer, not one computer to another.
T568B is the common wiring standard for twisted pair; with it on both ends, the cable is straight-through.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which connector is used for cable Internet?
explanation: Cable Internet connections use coaxial cable (usually RG-6) with an F-type connector on the end. The F-connector screws onto the cable modem or the wall jack.
whyWrong: LC is a small fiber optic connector, not a coaxial connector.
Direct burial is a type of cable for underground installations, not a connector.
RJ45 is the connector on twisted pair Ethernet patch cables.
DE-9 (often called DB9) is a serial connector used with RS-232 connections.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which cable type would be suitable for longer distances, such as connecting two cities?
explanation: Single-mode fiber is used for long-distance runs, for example from one city to the next, over distances as long as thousands of kilometers. Its thin core carries a single path of light, which keeps the signal clear over long distances.
whyWrong: Coaxial cable is common between utility poles and buildings, but it does not reach between cities.
Twisted pair is common in LANs and is limited to about 100 meters per run.
Multimode fiber has a wider core and is used for shorter runs, such as in server rooms and between campus buildings.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: You need to make a high-speed connection to an external storage device that can handle 40 Gbps. Which of the following is the BEST solution?
explanation: A Thunderbolt connection is the best solution, specifically Thunderbolt 3 or later, which can handle 40 Gbps over a USB-C connector. It is made for fast external storage and displays.
whyWrong: USB 3.2 is limited to 10 or 20 Gbps, even though it also uses the USB-C connector.
HDMI carries video and audio to displays, not data to storage devices.
Cat 6a is a twisted pair Ethernet cable rated for up to 10 Gbps, and it does not connect directly to a storage device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: Which of the following is the most common type of networking connector used in a PC’s network interface card?
explanation: The RJ45 connector is the most common networking connector. It is used on twisted pair Ethernet cables and on the network interface cards of PCs.
whyWrong: RJ11 is the connector used by landline telephones (POTS) and DSL connections.
The F-type connector is a coaxial connector for cable TV and cable Internet.
ST (straight tip) is a fiber optic connector that is not common on a PC's network interface card.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 3

stem: Which of the following cable types should be used to connect a cable modem to a SOHO router?
explanation: Use an Ethernet patch cable, such as Cat 5e or Cat 6, to connect a cable modem to a SOHO router. It is the same kind of patch cable that connects a computer to an RJ45 jack or a patch panel to a switch.
whyWrong: Coaxial (RG-6) cable connects the cable modem to the coaxial wall jack, not to the router.
USB cables connect peripherals to computers or charge devices, not a modem to a router.
Thunderbolt transmits data to devices or video to displays, not between a modem and a router.
SATA cables connect storage drives to a motherboard.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 12

stem: You need to connect external peripherals to a typical PC. Which of the following connector types will allow you to do this? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: External SATA (eSATA) is a SATA port meant for external devices, found on the back of some PCs or added with an adapter card. USB (3.0, 2.0, and others) is the most common port for external peripherals such as storage drives and audio and video equipment.
whyWrong: Standard SATA (without the e) connects internal devices, not external ones.
Serial Attached SCSI (SAS) is a drive technology for servers and power workstations, not typical PC peripherals.
EIDE (Parallel ATA) is an older internal drive standard.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 47

stem:
Look at the following list of wires. What wiring standard is being used here?

```
1. White/orange 2. Orange 3. White/green 4. Blue
5. White/blue   6. Green  7. White/brown 8. Brown
```
explanation: White/orange, orange, white/green, blue, white/blue, green, white/brown, brown is the pin order of the T568B wiring standard. A straight-through cable uses the same standard on both ends, and a crossover cable uses T568B on one end and T568A on the other.
whyWrong: RJ45 is the connector (plug or jack) on the cable, not a wiring standard.
T568A swaps the orange and green pairs, so it starts with white/green, green.
TIA is the standards organization that developed T568A and T568B, not a wiring standard itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 48

stem: Which of the following cable types is prone to EMI?
explanation: Unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cable has no shield, so it is prone to electromagnetic interference (EMI). Where EMI is a problem, use shielded twisted pair or fiber optic cable instead.
whyWrong: Fiber optic cable carries light instead of electricity, so EMI does not affect it.
Shielded twisted pair has a foil shield around the wires that protects against EMI.
Multimode is a type of optical fiber, which EMI does not affect.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 55

stem: Which of the following cable types would MOST LIKELY experience degraded video signal quality over long distances?
explanation: VGA is an older standard that sends analog signals to a monitor. Of the cables listed, it is the most susceptible to signal degradation over long distances.
whyWrong: HDMI sends digital signals, which hold their quality over longer distances than analog VGA.
DVI sends digital signals (DVI-D), which hold their quality better than analog VGA.
DisplayPort is a digital video interface that resists degradation better than analog VGA.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 62

stem: Which of the following ports can be used for audio, video, and storage?
explanation: Thunderbolt is the only listed port that carries audio, video, and storage data. It combines PCIe data and DisplayPort video on one cable, and newer versions use the USB-C connector.
whyWrong: DisplayPort carries audio and video but is not used for storage.
HDMI carries audio and video but is not used for storage.
DVI carries video only.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 71

stem: You have been hired to install a network cable in a crawl space that runs the length of a hallway. You are required to meet fire code specifications. Which of the following types of cable should you run?
explanation: You should run plenum-rated cable, whose special jacket does not burn, or burns more slowly, in a fire and gives off fewer toxic fumes. It is required in air-handling spaces such as crawl spaces and drop ceilings that a fire suppression system cannot reach.
whyWrong: Shielded cable such as STP reduces EMI but does not meet fire code for plenum spaces unless it is plenum-rated.
Coaxial cable is not a network cable for this run, and it does not meet fire code unless it is plenum-rated.
Fiber optic cable is fast but is not rated for plenum spaces by default.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 74

stem: Which of the following could be used with an analog monitor? (Choose two.)
explanation: Analog monitors require an analog signal. VGA is an analog video standard, and DVI-A is also analog; DVI-I would work as well.
whyWrong: HDMI is a digital standard and cannot drive an analog monitor directly.
DVI-D carries only digital signals.
DisplayPort is a digital standard.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 1

stem: You are attaching an external hard drive to a computer with USB 2.0 ports. The user is concerned about data transfer speed. What is the maximum speed of USB 2.0?
explanation: USB 2.0 has a maximum speed of 480 Mbps. USB 3.0 is 5 Gbps, USB 3.1 is 10 Gbps, USB 3.2 is 20 Gbps, and USB4 is up to 40 Gbps.
whyWrong: 5 Gbps is the speed of USB 3.0.
10 Gbps is the speed of USB 3.1.
20 Gbps is the speed of USB 3.2.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 2

stem: You got a new desktop computer for a designer at your company. On the front panel is a rectangular yellow USB port. What does that mean?
options: It's a port capable of charging devices even with the system powered off.
It's a port to be used with USB-C compatible devices.
explanation: A yellow USB port is an “always on” charging port that can charge devices even when the system is off. It could be either USB 2 or USB 3.
whyWrong: Port color does not mark USB 2.0; a yellow port can be USB 2 or USB 3.
USB 3.0 ports are usually blue; yellow marks an always-on charging port.
USB-C connectors are oval, not rectangular.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of the following connector types is typically not associated with hard drive use?
explanation: DB-9 connectors are most often used with serial cables and are not associated with hard drives. USB-C, eSATA, and SATA are examples of connectors used with hard drives.
whyWrong: USB-C is commonly used to connect external hard drives.
eSATA is a connector for external SATA hard drives.
SATA is the standard connector for internal hard drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 5

stem: The company photographer is interested in buying a new digital camera. He wants to be able to plug it directly into his laptop to transfer pictures for editing. What type of connector will MOST LIKELY be on his camera?
explanation: For smaller electronic devices such as cameras, micro-USB and mini-USB connectors are common. The other end of the cable is usually a standard USB connector that plugs into the laptop.
whyWrong: Thunderbolt is used primarily for video and high-speed peripherals on computers, not on cameras.
Molex is an internal power connector for drives.
Lightning is an Apple proprietary connector that has been replaced by USB-C on newer devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 6

stem: You are installing a new video card that has an HDMI port. Which of the following are true about HDMI cables? (Choose all that apply.)
options: They can transmit analog or digital signals.
They can transmit audio as well as video.
They are not used to connect to projectors.
They can use HDMI or mini-HDMI connectors.
explanation: HDMI cables transmit digital video and audio signals, and they can be used to connect to projectors or monitors. HDMI cables can have standard HDMI connectors, mini-HDMI connectors, or micro-HDMI connectors.
whyWrong: HDMI carries digital signals only, not analog.
HDMI cables are commonly used to connect projectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 7

stem: Which of the following display interfaces is equivalent to DisplayPort with PCIe added in?
explanation: Intel and Apple collaborated on Thunderbolt to add PCIe to VESA's DisplayPort and to make the resulting interface smaller and less expensive to connect. Thunderbolt can therefore carry both display and data traffic over one cable.
whyWrong: HDMI is a separate digital audio and video standard that does not include PCIe.
DVI is an older video interface that does not include PCIe.
VGA is an analog video interface that does not include PCIe.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 8

stem: Which two standards use the same connector? (Choose two.)
explanation: USB4 is based on the Thunderbolt 3 specifications, and both natively use USB-C connectors. USB-C is an oval connector that can be inserted either way up.
whyWrong: eSATA uses its own connector for external SATA drives.
USB 2.0 uses Type-A, Type-B, mini, or micro connectors, not USB-C natively.
Mini-USB is a small trapezoid connector, not the USB-C connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 9

stem: How do you connect a DVI-A interface on a peripheral to a DVI-D interface on the computer?
options: With a cable that is terminated on one end with a DVI-A connector and on the other end with a DVI-D connector.
You wouldn't interconnect those two interfaces.
explanation: Such a connection should not be made, because analog and digital DVI interfaces are too different to interconnect. DVI-I cables can connect two DVI-A or two DVI-D interfaces, but they cannot convert an analog signal to a digital one.
whyWrong: A DVI-I cable cannot convert the analog DVI-A signal into the digital signal that DVI-D needs.
A cable with a DVI-A end and a DVI-D end would not convert the signal, so the devices still could not communicate.
No standard DVI cable converts between analog and digital signals.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 10

stem: A technician says he needs to provide power to a PATA hard drive and a DVD-ROM in a desktop. The computer now has a new fully modular power supply, and the technician wants to know what type of power connectors he should take. What do you tell him?
explanation: A Molex connector is a power connector for IDE (PATA) storage devices. This includes hard drives and optical drives.
whyWrong: SATA power connectors are for SATA drives, not PATA drives.
SCSI is a drive interface, not a power connector.
Serial refers to a data cable and connector, not to drive power.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 11

stem: Which of the following connectors is oval shaped?
explanation: Thunderbolt 3 uses the oval-shaped USB-C connector. Thunderbolt 2 used a proprietary connector that was more of a square.
whyWrong: Micro-USB connectors are shaped more like a trapezoid than an oval.
Mini-USB connectors are shaped more like a trapezoid than an oval.
Thunderbolt 2 used a proprietary connector that was more of a square.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 12

stem: Which of the following connector types are capable of conducting power and transmitting data? (Choose all that apply.)
explanation: USB cables can transmit both power and data, and Lightning, USB-C, and micro-USB connectors are all found on the ends of USB cables. Some versions of eSATA cables (eSATAp) can also carry power along with data.
whyWrong: A Molex connector carries power only.
A DB-9 connector is used for serial cables and carries data only.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 13

stem: Which of the following statements is true about eSATA cables and connectors?
options: eSATA cables provide power and data to devices.
eSATA connectors are smaller than USB-C connectors.
eSATA is faster than USB4 and Thunderbolt 3.
explanation: The eSATA standards limit throughput to 6 Gbps, which is much slower than USB4 and Thunderbolt 3, both of which can reach 40 Gbps. Standard eSATA cables do not provide power, although some eSATA versions do.
whyWrong: Standard eSATA cables carry data only and do not provide power.
eSATA connectors are larger than USB-C connectors.
eSATA tops out at 6 Gbps, while USB4 and Thunderbolt 3 reach 40 Gbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 14

stem: Which of the following is not an example of a connector for a standard peripheral input device?
explanation: Peripherals most often use USB today, but they can also use D-sub connectors (rarely), and audio devices such as microphones and speakers use 1/8″ jacks. Molex connectors are power connectors for PATA hard drives and optical drives.
whyWrong: 1/8″ jacks are used by audio peripherals such as microphones and speakers.
D-sub connectors are still used, though rarely, by some peripheral devices.
USB is the most common connector for peripheral input devices today.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 15

stem: You are asked to hook up a projector in a classroom. What type of cable are you MOST LIKELY to need?
explanation: A projector uses a standard video cable, and in this case HDMI is the most likely choice. A projector might also have a USB interface, but HDMI is the best selection.
whyWrong: Some projectors have a USB interface, but USB Type A is not the usual video connection.
eSATA is for external hard drives, not video.
DB-9 is a slow serial connector, not a video connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 16

stem: A user with an iPhone 14 needs to charge her device and asks you to bring a cable. Which of the following connector types should you ensure that the cable has?
explanation: Starting with the iPhone 5 and ending with the iPhone 14 series, Apple iPhones used the proprietary Lightning connector for charging and connecting peripherals. From the iPhone 15 on, iPhones use USB-C instead.
whyWrong: Thunderbolt connectors are used on MacBooks for peripherals, not on iPhones.
iPhones do not have built-in mini-USB connectors.
iPhones do not have built-in micro-USB connectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 17
note: Book says Lightning ended with the iPhone 15; the iPhone 15 actually moved to USB-C, so the last Lightning iPhones were the iPhone 14 series. Explanation corrected; the question (iPhone 14) and answer are unaffected.

stem: Which of the following types of cables will transfer data at the slowest rate?
explanation: Classic serial ports and serial cables have the slowest data transmission speeds of these cable types. USB4 and Thunderbolt 3 reach 40 Gbps, and HDMI carries many gigabits per second of video.
whyWrong: USB4 can transfer data at up to 40 Gbps.
Thunderbolt 3 can transfer data at up to 40 Gbps.
HDMI carries high-bandwidth digital video and audio, far faster than serial.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 18

stem: What is the maximum data transfer rate of USB High Speed?
explanation: Full Speed USB is 12 Mbps and High Speed is 480 Mbps. SuperSpeed runs at 5 Gbps and SuperSpeed+ at 10 Gbps.
whyWrong: 10 Gbps is the speed of SuperSpeed+ USB.
5 Gbps is the speed of SuperSpeed USB.
12 Mbps is the speed of Full Speed USB.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 19

stem: VGA cables use what type of signal between the adapter and monitor?
explanation: VGA signals are analog, uncompressed, component signals that carry all of the video information for the three components of the original RGB signal. VGA uses a 15-pin D-sub connector.
whyWrong: VGA signals are analog, not digital.
VGA carries separate RGB component signals, not a composite signal.
VGA signals are not compressed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 3: Peripherals, Cables, and Connectors, Review Questions question 20

stem: ____________________ is immune to electromagnetic or radio-frequency interference.
explanation: Fiber-optic cable carries data as pulses of light, so it is not affected by electromagnetic or radio-frequency interference. Even though some copper cables have shielding, they are not immune to EMI or RFI.
whyWrong: Twisted pair cabling is copper, and even shielded twisted pair can still pick up EMI and RFI.
CSMA/CD is a media access method, not a cable type.
Broadband coaxial cabling is copper, so its shielding reduces interference but does not make it immune.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which of the following is a type of connector used with coaxial cable?
explanation: Coaxial cable uses F-type connectors, which screw on and are common for cable television and cable modems. Older coaxial networks also used BNC connectors.
whyWrong: RJ11 is a small twisted pair connector used for telephone lines and DSL.
RJ45 is the eight-pin twisted pair connector used for Ethernet.
SC is a square, snap-in fiber-optic connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 2

stem: You need to put a connector on the end of an Ethernet crossover cable. The existing end has a white and green colored wire at pin 1. What color do you need to make pin 1 on the new end?
explanation: A crossover cable swaps the transmit and receive pairs, so pins 1 and 3 (and pins 2 and 6) trade places between the two ends. If one end has white/green at pin 1, the other end needs white/orange at pin 1. In effect, one end is wired to T568A and the other to T568B.
whyWrong: White/green at pin 1 on both ends would make a straight-through cable, not a crossover cable.
Solid green belongs at pin 2 or pin 6, never at pin 1.
Solid orange sits at pin 2 in T568B (or pin 6 in T568A), not at pin 1.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 3

stem: What is the lowest grade of UTP that is rated for 100 Mbps transmission?
explanation: Cat 5 was the first UTP standard ratified for 100 Mbps transmissions. Before that, Cat 3 was popular but supported only 10 Mbps. Cat 5e, Cat 6, and Cat 6a all support at least 1 Gbps and came after Cat 5.
whyWrong: Cat 5e supports 1 Gbps, so it is not the lowest grade rated for 100 Mbps.
Cat 6 supports 1 Gbps and 10 Gbps over shorter runs, well above the lowest grade for 100 Mbps.
Cat 6a supports 10 Gbps up to 100 meters and is a much later, higher grade.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 5

stem: An administrator needs to run a network cable between two buildings that are about 150 yards apart on a campus. Company regulations say the cable must be underground. What type of cable should the administrator use?
explanation: Direct burial cable is designed to be buried underground, as its name implies. Its jacket resists water, soil, and temperature changes, and the cable inside can be fiber-optic or copper.
whyWrong: Fiber-optic cable can cover the distance, but a standard fiber jacket is not made to be buried without a direct burial rating.
STP adds shielding against interference but is not made to be buried in the ground.
Plenum cable is fire-resistant cable for spaces that circulate breathable air inside a building.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 6

stem: Of all the network cabling options, ___________________ offers the longest possible segment length.
explanation: Fiber-optic cable can span distances of several kilometers because it has much lower attenuation, crosstalk, and interference than copper cable. Single-mode fiber (SMF) can run longer distances than multimode fiber (MMF).
whyWrong: Unshielded twisted pair Ethernet is limited to about 100 meters per segment.
Coaxial cable runs farther than twisted pair but nowhere near the kilometers that fiber reaches.
Multimode fiber uses a wider core and is limited to shorter runs than single-mode fiber.
Shielded twisted pair Ethernet has the same 100-meter limit as UTP.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 7

stem: If you are going to run a network cable in the space above the drop ceiling in your office, which type of cable should you use?
explanation: For areas where a cable must be fire retardant, such as the space above a drop ceiling, you must run plenum-grade cable. Plenum refers to the coating on the sleeve of the cable, not the copper or fiber within the cable itself.
whyWrong: PVC is the other common cable coating, but it produces poisonous gas when it burns, so it is not allowed in air-handling spaces.
Coaxial describes the cable's construction, and a standard coaxial jacket is not fire rated for plenum spaces.
Fiber-optic describes the conductor, and fiber still needs a plenum-rated jacket in that space.
Direct burial cable is designed to be buried underground, not run through ceiling air spaces.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 12

stem: Which of the following connector types is an MFF connector?
explanation: The Lucent connector (LC) is a mini form factor (MFF) fiber-optic connector developed by Lucent Technologies. It is about half the size of an SC connector, so more ports fit on a switch or patch panel; some remember it as the "little connector."
whyWrong: BNC is a twist-lock connector for coaxial copper cable, not a mini form factor fiber connector.
ST is a full-size round fiber connector with a bayonet twist lock.
SC is a full-size square fiber connector that snaps in place.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 13

stem: What Ethernet specification would you be running if you needed to make a connection of 10 Gbps over a distance of five kilometers?
explanation: A 5-kilometer connection limits you to fiber-optic cable, specifically single-mode fiber (SMF). Two common 10 Gbps SMF standards are 10GBaseER and 10GBaseEW, where the E stands for extended reach.
whyWrong: The T in 10GBaseT means twisted pair copper, which reaches only about 100 meters.
10GBaseSR (short reach) runs over multimode fiber and covers only a few hundred meters.
A DR (distance reach) fiber standard does not stretch to 5 kilometers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 14
note: Ethernet naming standards (10GBaseER and others) are not named in the 220-1201 objectives; tagged to optical single-mode cable under 3.2.

stem: Which type of fiber-optic cable connector uses a twist to lock mechanism to secure the cable in place?
explanation: A straight tip (ST) connector uses a bayonet twist-to-lock mechanism to hold the fiber in place. SC and LC connectors snap in instead.
whyWrong: BNC also twists to lock, but it is a connector for coaxial copper cable, not fiber.
SC is a square fiber connector that snaps in place rather than twisting.
LC is a small fiber connector with a latch that snaps in place.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 16

stem: What type of coaxial cable is recommended for digital television cable signals?
explanation: The two RG standards used for cable television are RG-6 and RG-59. Of the two, RG-6 is better because it can run longer distances and can handle digital signals, while RG-59 is suited to analog signals.
whyWrong: RG-8 is thick Ethernet (thicknet) coax, not a cable television standard.
RG-58 is thin Ethernet (thinnet) coax, not a cable television standard.
RG-59 is a cable television coax for analog signals and shorter runs, not the recommended choice for digital.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which type of networking device uses bare wires for attachments rather than a connector?
explanation: A punchdown block connects bare wires to its frame to make a network connection, with no connector on that end of the cable. The wires are pressed into the block's slots with a punchdown tool.
whyWrong: A patch panel uses RJ45 or other connectors on its front side.
A PoE injector connects with RJ45 network cables, not bare wires.
An access point connects wireless clients and uses a standard network jack for its wired link.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 6: Networking Fundamentals, Review Questions question 20
note: Punchdown block is listed under 3.2 connector types; the punchdown tool is 2.8. Kept in Domain 3.

stem: What voltages should the two traditionally colored hot wires on a Molex connector read?
explanation: A Molex connector's red wire should read 5 volts, and the yellow wire should read 12 volts. The black wires are ground.
whyWrong: Molex connectors carry 5 V and 12 V, not 3.3 V.
The colors are reversed: red is 5 V and yellow is 12 V.
Molex connectors carry no 3.3 V wire, and yellow is 12 V.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 7: Power Supplies, Chapter Review question 6

stem: How many pins does a SATA power connector have?
explanation: SATA power connectors have 15 pins. The SATA data connector, by contrast, has 7 pins.
whyWrong: 6 pins is the count of some PCIe power connectors, not SATA power.
9 pins is not the SATA power pin count.
12 pins is not the SATA power pin count.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 7: Power Supplies, Chapter Review question 10
note: Older book (220-1101/1102), All-in-One 11e Chapter 7: power connectors. Mapped to SATA cables and motherboard power connectors.

stem: What is the maximum cable length of an internal SATA device?
explanation: The maximum cable length of an internal SATA device is 1 meter. External eSATA cables can be up to 2 meters long.
whyWrong: 2 meters is the eSATA maximum, not the internal SATA maximum.
12 inches is shorter than the SATA limit.
18 inches was the old PATA ribbon cable limit, not the SATA limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 6

stem: What is the maximum number of SATA drives you can have on a system?
options: There is no maximum other than the limitations of your motherboard/host card.
explanation: There is no maximum number of SATA drives you can have on a system beyond the limits imposed by the number of ports on your motherboard or host card. Each SATA drive connects to its own port.
whyWrong: SATA has no one-drive limit; each port takes one drive.
Two drives per channel was the old PATA limit, not a SATA limit.
Many motherboards have more or fewer than eight ports; SATA itself sets no limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 7

stem: What happens to bus speed and power usage when you plug multiple devices into a USB hub?
options: The bus speed stays constant, but power usage increases.
The bus speed increases because each device brings a little burst; power usage increases.
The bus speed decreases because all devices share the same total bandwidth; power usage increases.
The bus speed decreases because all devices share the same total bandwidth; power usage decreases.
explanation: When you plug multiple devices into a USB hub, the bus speed decreases because all devices share the same total bandwidth, and power usage increases. Each added device draws power from the hub or its port.
whyWrong: The bus speed does not stay constant, because the devices share the bandwidth.
Adding devices never increases the bus speed; they split the same bandwidth.
Power usage goes up, not down, as more devices draw power.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which cable is used to transfer information between two devices using a serial communication protocol?
explanation: A serial cable transfers information between two devices using a serial communication protocol. Older serial ports often use the DB9 connector.
whyWrong: Thunderbolt is a high-speed interface that carries PCIe and DisplayPort data, not a classic serial cable.
A video cable carries display signals to a monitor.
A hard drive cable connects storage drives to the motherboard or controller.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 3

stem: You take a tech call from a user who complains that she gets an error message, “Hub power exceeded,” when she plugs her new thumb drive into her USB keyboard’s external USB port. Worse, the device won’t work. What’s MOST LIKELY the problem?
options: She has a defective thumb drive.
She plugged a Hi-Speed device into a Full-Speed port.
She plugged one too many devices into the USB hub.
explanation: Just like the error message said, the thumb drive drew too much power for the hub to handle. A keyboard's built-in USB port is usually an unpowered hub that can supply only a little power, so plug the drive into a port on the computer or a powered hub.
whyWrong: The message names the hub's power limit, not a defective port.
A defective drive would not cause the hub to report that its power was exceeded.
Plugging a Hi-Speed device into a Full-Speed port only makes it run slower; it does not exceed hub power.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 4
note: Older book (220-1101/1102), All-in-One 11e Chapter 10: USB troubleshooting. Mapped to peripheral cables (USB).

stem: What is the fastest speed that Hi-Speed USB 2.0 can go?
explanation: Hi-Speed USB 2.0 has a theoretical maximum of 480 Mbps. USB 3.0 SuperSpeed raised the maximum to 5 Gbps.
whyWrong: 12 Mbps is the Full-Speed USB 1.1 rate.
120 Mbps is not a USB speed rating.
400 Mbps is the speed of FireWire 400, not USB 2.0.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 5

stem: What is the maximum cable length for USB 2.0?
explanation: USB 2.0 has a maximum cable length of 5 meters. Longer runs need a hub or an active extension cable.
whyWrong: 1.2 meters is shorter than the USB 2.0 limit.
The limit is set in meters, and 1.2 yards is much shorter than it.
5 feet is about 1.5 meters, far shorter than the 5-meter limit.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 6

stem: While he’s at his desk, Dudley wants to connect his MacBook Air (which has a pair of Thunderbolt 3 ports) to a flat-panel monitor, USB mouse, and USB keyboard. Which of the following could meet his need?
options: A monitor with at least two built-in USB ports and a USB Type-C upstream port
One Thunderbolt-to-DisplayPort adapter and two Thunderbolt-to-USB adapters
explanation: If Dudley gets a monitor with at least two USB ports and a USB Type-C upstream port, he can connect the display, mouse, and keyboard all to a single Thunderbolt port on his MacBook Air. Thunderbolt 3 uses the USB Type-C connector, so one USB-C cable carries both the video signal and the USB data to the monitor's built-in hub.
whyWrong: USB adapters alone give no way to connect the monitor, which needs a video signal.
A KVM switch shares one keyboard, monitor, and mouse among several computers; it does not add ports to one laptop.
Three adapters need three ports, but the MacBook Air has only two Thunderbolt ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Depending on version, Thunderbolt ports manifest as one of which two connector formats?
explanation: Thunderbolt 1 and 2 both use the Mini DisplayPort connector, while Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use the USB Type-C connector. A Thunderbolt port can carry video and data on the same cable.
whyWrong: Thunderbolt has never used the full-size DisplayPort connector.
Thunderbolt does not use either full-size DisplayPort or Mini HDMI.
Mini HDMI is a small HDMI video connector and was never used for Thunderbolt.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 17: Display Technologies, Chapter Review question 7

stem: What is the minimum Cat level cable required for a 1000BASE-T network?
explanation: Cat 5e is the minimum cable rating for reliable 1000BASE-T (Gigabit Ethernet). Plain Cat 5 is rated for 100 Mbps, and Cat 5e added tighter specifications for gigabit speeds.
whyWrong: Cat 1 is old voice-grade telephone wire that cannot carry Ethernet data.
Cat 5 is rated for 100 Mbps; Cat 5e is the minimum rating for reliable gigabit Ethernet.
Cat 6 supports 1000BASE-T, but it is more than the minimum.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 2
note: Book explanation said 'Cat 5 or better', which contradicts its own answer (Cat 5e); the explanation follows the answer and the current books (Cat 5 = 100 Mbps, Cat 5e = 1 Gbps).

stem: A typical Cat 6 cable uses which connector?
explanation: Cat 6 cables use an RJ45 connector. RJ45 is the 8-pin connector used on twisted pair Ethernet cables.
whyWrong: RJ11 is the smaller 4-pin connector used for telephone lines and DSL.
Plenum is a fire rating for the cable jacket, not a connector.
PVC is a cable jacket material, not a connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Why would you use STP over UTP cabling?
explanation: Shielded twisted pair (STP) cabling handles interference from other electronics much better than unshielded twisted pair (UTP). Use it near motors, lights, and other sources of electromagnetic interference.
whyWrong: STP costs more than UTP because of its extra shielding.
The shielding and grounding make STP harder to install than UTP.
STP and UTP are different cable types: one has shielding and the other does not.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 5

stem: John’s boss asks for a recommendation for connecting the company network to a small satellite building about 1 km from the main campus. The company owns the verdant land in between. Given such a scenario, what network technology implementation should John suggest?
explanation: John should suggest Ethernet over single-mode fiber, the only option listed that can cover 1 km. Single-mode fiber can carry signals for many kilometers, while copper twisted pair is limited to about 100 meters.
whyWrong: UTP Ethernet is limited to runs of about 100 meters.
STP Ethernet has the same 100-meter limit as UTP.
Multimode fiber reaches only a few hundred meters at gigabit speeds, so 1 km is beyond it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 8

stem: Erin is purchasing cable for the horizontal runs in a new office. What type of UTP cable should Erin order?
explanation: Erin should buy plenum/solid-core cable because horizontal runs go through the walls and ceilings (the plenum space) of the office. Plenum-rated cable gives off less toxic smoke in a fire, and solid-core cable carries signals better over long fixed runs.
whyWrong: Stranded-core, non-plenum cable is for patch cables, not for runs inside walls and ceilings.
Stranded-core cable is flexible but is meant for patch cables, not for horizontal runs.
Non-plenum cable may not meet fire code in the plenum space where horizontal runs go.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 9

stem: Eddard hands Will a cable. Will hands it back and says, meaningfully, “That’s a nice F-type connector you’ve got there.” What kind of cable does Eddard have?
explanation: Eddard has a coaxial cable. The screw-on F-type connector is used on coaxial cable for cable modems and TV.
whyWrong: Fiber optic cable uses connectors such as SC, ST, or LC, not F-type.
STP cable uses RJ45 connectors.
UTP cable uses RJ45 or RJ11 connectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 18: Essentials of Networking, Chapter Review question 10

stem: What type of interface uses a nine-pin RS-232 hardware port?
explanation: Serial devices use the nine-pin RS-232 port (DB-9). It was used by legacy mice, printers, and modems, and it is still found on networking equipment as a console port.
whyWrong: Parallel connections use a larger 25-pin port and were used mostly by legacy printers.
RJ45 is the connector used by Ethernet cables.
RJ11 connects a modem or phone to a telephone line.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 1: Mobile Devices, Objective 1.3 question 12
note: Neil chapter 1, old objective 220-1101/1.3; current 3.2 peripheral cables (serial).

stem: An organization using unshielded twisted pair cabling has been suffering from Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). What can the organization implement to protect from EMI and also provide high-speed communication at the same time?
explanation: Fiber-optic cable carries light pulses instead of electrical signals, so it is immune to EMI. It also gives the highest speeds and longest distances.
whyWrong: Coaxial cable resists some EMI but is slower than fiber for network links.
Shielded twisted pair reduces EMI but is still copper and does not match fiber's speed.
10BASE-T is a legacy 10 Mbps Ethernet standard over twisted pair.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.7 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 2.7 set; cable types and EMI are now under 220-1201 3.2 Network cables.

stem: What is the main limitation of using copper cables for high-speed data transmission?
explanation: Copper cables are subject to signal attenuation, which is the loss of signal strength over distance. This is why twisted pair Ethernet runs are limited to 100 meters.
whyWrong: Copper can pick up electromagnetic interference, which reduces speed, but this is not its main limitation.
Bandwidth limits the overall capacity of a link but is not the main problem with copper at high speeds.
Insulation problems cause signal quality faults but do not set the basic limit of copper cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 1

stem: What is the maximum distance limitation of Cat 5 cables for Ethernet networking?
explanation: Cat 5 cables for Ethernet have a maximum segment length of 100 meters. The same 100-meter limit applies to the other twisted pair categories used for Ethernet.
whyWrong: 150 meters is beyond the 100-meter limit for twisted pair Ethernet.
200 meters is twice the supported length of a Cat 5 run.
250 meters is far beyond the 100-meter limit for Cat 5.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 4

stem: In which of the following scenarios would you use an RJ11 connector?
options: Connecting a telephone handset to a wall jack
Connecting a computer to a router
Connecting a TV to a cable box
explanation: RJ11 connectors are used for telephone lines, for example to connect a telephone handset or a DSL modem to a wall jack. They are smaller than RJ45 connectors and usually carry two or four wires.
whyWrong: A computer connects to a router with an RJ45 Ethernet connector, not RJ11.
Printers usually connect with USB or with an RJ45 Ethernet connector.
A TV connects to a cable box with HDMI or with a coaxial cable and F-type connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 6

stem: When using a Gigabit network card, what is the maximum data transmission speed limitation of Cat 5 cables?
explanation: Cat 5 cable is rated for a maximum of 100 Mbps, so it limits a Gigabit network card to Fast Ethernet speed. Cat 5e and Cat 6 are rated for 1 Gbps.
whyWrong: 1 Gbps needs Cat 5e or better cable.
10 Gbps needs Cat 6a cable for a full 100-meter run.
40 Gbps is the speed of Cat 8 cable over short runs.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 7

stem: Which operating system commonly utilizes Thunderbolt cables for high-speed data transfer and device connectivity?
explanation: Thunderbolt was developed by Intel together with Apple, and it is most closely associated with Apple Mac computers. It carries high-speed data, video, and power over one cable.
whyWrong: Many Windows PCs support Thunderbolt, but the interface is most associated with Apple Macs.
Linux can use Thunderbolt devices, but it is not the system most associated with the interface.
Android phones and tablets use USB-C or micro-USB ports, not Thunderbolt.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 8
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.1 (cables and connectors).

stem: In which scenario would you commonly use a Lightning to USB cable?
options: Connecting a printer to a computer
Connecting a monitor to a laptop
explanation: A Lightning to USB cable is used to charge and sync an iPhone or other Apple mobile device that has a Lightning port. The USB end connects to a charger or a computer.
whyWrong: Printers connect to computers with USB or Ethernet cables, not Lightning.
Two computers are connected with an Ethernet (crossover) cable or a network, not a Lightning cable.
A monitor connects to a laptop with a video cable such as HDMI, DisplayPort, or USB-C.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 10

stem: What type of cable has a T568B connection on one end and a T568A connection on the other end?
explanation: A crossover cable has the T568A wiring standard on one end and T568B on the other, which swaps the transmit and receive pairs. It connects two similar devices, for example two computers or two switches.
whyWrong: A straight-through cable uses the same wiring standard, T568A or T568B, on both ends.
Coaxial cable has one center conductor and uses F-type or BNC connectors, not T568 wiring.
Fiber optic cable carries light and uses connectors such as SC, ST, or LC, not T568 wiring.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 11

stem: What is the actual speed difference between USB and USB 2?
options: USB offers a speed of 12 Mbps, while USB 2 offers a speed of 480 Mbps
USB and USB 2 have the same speed of 480 Mbps
USB 2 offers a speed of 12 Mbps, while USB offers a speed of 480 Mbps
USB and USB 2 have variable speeds depending on the version
explanation: The original USB (USB 1.1) runs at up to 12 Mbps, while USB 2.0 Hi-Speed runs at up to 480 Mbps. USB 3.0 later raised the speed to 5 Gbps.
whyWrong: USB 1.1 is limited to 12 Mbps, so the two versions do not share the same speed.
This reverses the two versions: USB 2.0 is the faster one at 480 Mbps.
Each USB version has a defined maximum speed; the speeds are not variable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 12

stem: When should plenum-grade cables be used in networking installations?
explanation: Plenum-grade cables have a fire-resistant jacket that gives off less toxic smoke when it burns. Fire codes require them in air-handling spaces such as the space above a drop ceiling.
whyWrong: Outdoor runs need cable rated for outdoor or direct burial use, not plenum cable.
Plenum cable supports the same data speeds as non-plenum cable of the same category.
The plenum rating is about fire safety, not about longer distances.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 13

stem: When would you use Shielded Twisted Pair (STP) cables in networking installations?
explanation: Shielded twisted pair (STP) cable has a metal shield that keeps electromagnetic interference (EMI) from disrupting the signal. It is used near motors, fluorescent lights, and other EMI sources.
whyWrong: Outdoor installations need cable rated for outdoor or direct burial use; shielding alone is not the reason to use STP.
STP has the same 100-meter Ethernet limit as UTP, so it does not help with long distances.
In a low-EMI environment, cheaper unshielded twisted pair (UTP) cable is enough.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 14

stem: When are F-type connectors commonly used in networking?
explanation: F-type connectors are threaded coaxial connectors used for cable television (CATV) and cable modem connections. They screw onto the coaxial port of a TV, cable box, or modem.
whyWrong: Ethernet network connections use RJ45 connectors.
Fiber optic connections use connectors such as SC, ST, or LC.
Wi-Fi devices connect wirelessly through antennas, not through an F-type cable connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 15

stem: You are setting up a fiber optic network and need to choose between SC and LC connectors. Which connector type provides a higher density and is commonly used in data centers?
explanation: LC connectors have a small form factor, so many of them fit in a small space. This high density makes them common in data centers and other places where rack space matters.
whyWrong: SC connectors are widely used but are about twice the size of LC connectors.
ST connectors are older, larger bayonet-style connectors that do not give high density.
FC connectors are large threaded connectors used mainly in specialized and industrial settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 17

stem: Which of the following interfaces is commonly used to connect external storage devices to a computer at high speeds?
explanation: eSATA (External Serial ATA) is designed to connect external storage devices such as hard drives at SATA speeds of up to 6 Gbps. Its port is shielded and sturdier than an internal SATA port.
whyWrong: USB 2.0 is limited to 480 Mbps, much slower than eSATA.
HDMI carries audio and video to displays and TVs, not storage data.
VGA is an old analog video interface for monitors and projectors.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.1 question 18

stem: How can you identify a SATA cable used in computer hardware?
options: It has a small, L-shaped connector at one end and a flat connector at the other end
It has a wide, rectangular connector at both ends
It has a round, barrel-shaped connector at one end and a flat connector at the other end
It has a triangular-shaped connector at one end and a small, rectangular connector at the other end
explanation: A SATA data cable is a thin, flat cable with a small, L-shaped (keyed) 7-pin connector. The L shape makes sure the connector goes in only one way.
whyWrong: Wide rectangular connectors at both ends describe the old 40-pin IDE (PATA) ribbon cable.
A round barrel-shaped connector is a power connector, not a SATA connector.
SATA connectors are not triangular; this shape does not describe any drive cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 7
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.3 (storage).

stem: Which of the following options correctly describes a Molex connector?
options: The Molex connector is used to provide power to SATA drives
The Molex connector is primarily used for connecting fans and cooling devices
The Molex connector is a standard power connector for motherboards
The Molex connector is used to connect USB devices to the computer
explanation: The 4-pin Molex connector is a peripheral power connector that gives 5V and 12V. It powers fans and other cooling devices and, in older systems, PATA hard drives and optical drives.
whyWrong: SATA drives use the 15-pin SATA power connector, not Molex.
The standard motherboard power connector is the 20+4-pin ATX connector.
USB devices connect through USB ports; Molex carries only power.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.4 question 20
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.4 (motherboards, CPUs, add-on cards).

stem: Which type of USB connector is commonly used for connecting printers to a computer?
explanation: A USB printer cable has a Type A connector on the computer end and a square Type B connector on the printer end. The Type B connector is the one that identifies a printer connection.
whyWrong: Type A is the computer end of the cable; the printer itself has a Type B port.
Some new printers have USB-C, but the standard printer connector is Type B.
Micro-USB is used for mobile devices, not for printers.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 2
