note: Book answer Type A corrected to Type B: printers have a USB Type B port, and Type A is only the computer end of the cable. Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: What is the maximum data transfer rate supported by USB 2.0?
explanation: USB 2.0 (Hi-Speed USB) supports a maximum data transfer rate of 480 Mbps. It is commonly used for keyboards, mice, printers, and external storage.
whyWrong: No USB version is rated at 1 Gbps; that is the rate of Gigabit Ethernet.
5 Gbps is the rate of USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1), not USB 2.0.
10 Gbps is the rate of USB 3.1 Gen 2 (USB 3.2 Gen 2), not USB 2.0.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 42
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is the maximum data transfer rate supported by USB 3.0?
explanation: USB 3.0, also known as USB 3.1 Gen 1 and USB 3.2 Gen 1, supports a maximum data transfer rate of 5 Gbps. This is more than ten times faster than USB 2.0.
whyWrong: 480 Mbps is the maximum rate of USB 2.0.
1 Gbps is not a USB rate; it is the rate of Gigabit Ethernet.
10 Gbps is the rate of USB 3.1 Gen 2 (USB 3.2 Gen 2).
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 43
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is the maximum data transfer rate typically supported by Fast Ethernet (100BASE-TX) technology?
explanation: Fast Ethernet, also known as 100BASE-TX, supports a maximum data transfer rate of 100 Mbps. It was a common standard for wired connections in homes and small businesses.
whyWrong: 10 Mbps is the rate of 10BASE-T, an older Ethernet standard.
1 Gbps is the rate of Gigabit Ethernet (1000BASE-T).
10 Gbps is the rate of 10 Gigabit Ethernet (10GBASE-T).
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 46
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which Ethernet standard supports a maximum data transfer rate of 10 gigabits per second (Gbps)?
explanation: 10 Gigabit Ethernet (10GBASE-T) supports a maximum data transfer rate of 10 Gbps. It is used in enterprise networks and data centers that need high bandwidth, over Cat 6 (short runs) or Cat 6a cable.
whyWrong: 10BASE-T is an old standard with a maximum rate of 10 Mbps.
100BASE-TX (Fast Ethernet) supports a maximum of 100 Mbps.
Gigabit Ethernet (1000BASE-T) supports a maximum of 1 Gbps.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 47
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is the maximum data transfer rate supported by the Cat 5 cable?
explanation: Cat 5 cable supports a maximum data transfer rate of 100 Mbps (Fast Ethernet). Cat 5e and later categories are needed for faster speeds.
whyWrong: 10 Mbps is the rate of older standards such as 10BASE-T, and Cat 5 supports more than that.
1 Gbps needs Cat 5e or better.
10 Gbps needs Cat 6 (short runs) or Cat 6a.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 48
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is the transfer rate of DDR4-2133?
explanation: The transfer rate of DDR4-2133 is 17,066 MB/s, so the module is also known as PC4-17000. The rate is the number of transfers per second (2133 million) times the 8-byte (64-bit) bus width.
whyWrong: 19,200 MB/s is the transfer rate of DDR4-2400 (PC4-19200).
21,333 MB/s is the transfer rate of DDR4-2666 (PC4-21333).
25,600 MB/s is the transfer rate of DDR4-3200 (PC4-25600).
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: A technician attempts to install a DDR5 module into a motherboard, but it doesn’t appear to fit. Which of the following are possible reasons for this? (Select the two best answers.)
options: The motherboard doesn’t allow DDR5 memory.
The RAM stick is being installed backward.
explanation: The motherboard might accept only DDR4, and DDR memory is not backward compatible, so a DDR5 module does not fit a DDR4 slot. The module might also be turned around; always line up the notch on the module with the key in the slot.
whyWrong: The operating system cannot stop a module from physically fitting into a slot.
A BIOS/UEFI update does not change the shape of the slot, so it cannot cause a physical fit problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following technologies allows for a 256-bit-wide bus?
explanation: Quad-channel memory architecture allows a 256-bit-wide bus, 64 bits for each of the four channels. You get the full width only when all four channels have memory installed.
whyWrong: ECC (error-correcting code) detects and corrects memory errors; it does not widen the bus.
Virtual RAM uses storage to extend usable memory and has nothing to do with the memory bus width.
Task Manager is a Windows tool for viewing system performance, not a memory technology.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: A technician has just installed additional RAM into a Windows-based graphics-intensive workstation to meet software application requirements. What should the technician do NEXT to ensure that the correct amount of RAM is installed and that it is working properly? (Select the two best answers.)
options: Increase the size of the paging file.
Press down with both thumbs until the ears lock.
explanation: The most important thing to do after installation is to test the RAM. Check that the BIOS/UEFI recognizes the new RAM as the right type and speed, and then view the amount of RAM in the operating system; in Windows, go to Settings > System > About.
whyWrong: The paging file (virtual memory) uses part of the storage drive to extend RAM; resizing it does not confirm the new modules work.
Pressing the module down until the ears lock is part of the installation, which the scenario says is already done.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A technician has installed dual-inline memory modules that each have 288 pins and use 1.1 V. What kind of RAM has the tech installed?
explanation: DDR5 DIMMs have 288 pins and operate at 1.1 V. DDR4 DIMMs also have 288 pins, but they use a different notch position and 1.2 V, so the two are not interchangeable.
whyWrong: DDR4 DIMMs have 288 pins, but they run at 1.2 V, not 1.1 V.
DDR3 DIMMs have 240 pins and run at 1.5 V (1.35 V for DDR3L).
DDR4 SODIMMs are laptop modules with 260 pins, not 288.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A technician is considering RAM types for a server where mission-critical applications are run and errors can be detrimental. What type of RAM is currently the BEST option for the tech to consider installing in the server?
explanation: ECC RAM detects and corrects memory errors, so it is typically used in servers where mission-critical applications run and errors can be detrimental. Most consumer desktop motherboards do not even support ECC RAM.
whyWrong: Non-ECC RAM is fine for most consumer computers, but it cannot correct memory errors.
Virtual RAM is space on a storage drive that emulates RAM; it adds no error protection.
DDR6 is still in development and is not available to install today.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 14: RAM, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which of the following is the bus width of quad-channel RAM?
explanation: The bus width of quad-channel RAM is 256 bits: four 64-bit channels working together. In this configuration four modules (or eight or more) work at the same time.
whyWrong: 64-bit is the width of single-channel memory.
128-bit is the width of dual-channel memory.
288-pin is the module connection type of DDR4 and DDR5 DIMMs, not a bus width.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 4

stem: As you are building a new PC, you notice that the motherboard has eight DIMM sockets that are labeled 0 through 7. Four of them are gray, and the other four are a darker shade of gray. Which of the following should be performed FIRST?
options: Install the memory into the gray slots.
Install the memory into the dark gray slots.
Install the memory into slots 0 through 3.
Fill all the slots with memory.
explanation: Always check the motherboard documentation before you install components. It shows which memory type to use, which channel configuration (such as dual- or quad-channel) the board supports, and which slots to fill for each configuration. Slot colors and numbering differ between manufacturers, so the manual is the only reliable guide.
whyWrong: The gray slots might be the right ones for a multichannel setup, but you cannot know without the documentation.
The dark gray slots might be the secondary slot of each channel, so using them first could be wrong.
Slot numbers do not always match channels; many boards label slots A1, A2, B1, B2, and so on.
Filling every slot is expensive, probably unnecessary, and still needs the right memory for the board.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 39

stem: Which of the following memory technologies enables protection against random inconsistencies when storing data?
explanation: ECC (error-correcting code) memory detects and corrects common types of data corruption in RAM. It is often used in servers and in other systems where data corruption cannot be tolerated.
whyWrong: Quad-channel means the RAM sends data over four 64-bit channels at once; it does not correct errors.
Parity memory can detect some errors but cannot correct them the way ECC does.
Dual-channel means the RAM uses two 64-bit channels at once; it does not correct errors.
RAID 5 is a redundant storage drive array, not a memory technology.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 65

stem: You are told by a technician over the phone that you need to bring replacement DDR4 SDRAM memory. What type of packaging is used for DDR4 SDRAM memory?
explanation: DDR4 SDRAM is manufactured on a 288-pin DIMM, as is DDR5, although the two are keyed differently and are not compatible. DIMMs with 240 pins are used for DDR2 and DDR3 SDRAM.
whyWrong: No DIMM standard uses 224 pins.
240-pin DIMMs are used for DDR2 and DDR3 SDRAM, not DDR4.
No DIMM standard uses 296 pins.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 2

stem: You need to replace memory in a server that is using ECC RAM. Which of the following statements regarding the replacement RAM is true?
options: Installing non-ECC RAM will work fine, but the new RAM won't have error-correcting.
You can only install ECC RAM for it to work properly.
You can install non-ECC RAM and it will adapt for error-correction.
Installing non-ECC RAM will work fine as long as the new RAM includes a parity bit.
explanation: If a system requires ECC RAM, then only ECC RAM will work. Non-ECC RAM does not have error-correcting capabilities, and modern RAM does not use a separate parity bit.
whyWrong: A system that requires ECC RAM will not work properly with non-ECC modules.
Non-ECC RAM cannot adapt itself to provide error correction.
Modern RAM modules no longer use parity bits, and parity is not a substitute for the ECC the server requires.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 3

stem: You are training new technicians to install RAM and pointing out differences between packages. Which of the following are the numbers of pins that can be found on DIMM modules used in desktop motherboards? (Choose two.)
explanation: DIMMs used in desktop motherboards have one of four possible pin counts. SDR SDRAM is implemented on 168-pin modules and DDR SDRAM on 184-pin modules. DDR2 and DDR3 are implemented on 240-pin modules with different keying, and DDR4 and DDR5 DIMMs have 288 pins with different keying.
whyWrong: No memory modules use 180 pins.
200-pin modules are part of the SODIMM line used in laptops.
204-pin modules are part of the SODIMM line used in laptops.
232-pin modules were an older dual-channel design, not one of the standard desktop SDRAM DIMM pin counts.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 11

stem: The 32 GB of DDR4 memory has failed in a client's desktop computer. The client requests that you upgrade the system for better performance when replacing the RAM. Which of the following is the BEST option?
options: Install two new 32 GB DDR4 RAM modules.
Install two new 128 GB DDR4 RAM modules.
Install two new 32 GB DDR5 RAM modules.
Install two new 128 GB DDR5 RAM modules.
explanation: The only viable option listed is to install two new 32 GB DDR4 RAM modules. Check the motherboard documentation first to make sure the system will support that much memory. DDR5 is not compatible with DDR4 motherboards.
whyWrong: 128 GB DDR4 modules are not made as standard desktop modules, and a desktop board would not support them.
DDR5 modules are keyed differently and will not fit a DDR4 motherboard.
DDR5 modules will not fit a DDR4 motherboard, whatever their size.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 18
note: Book says DDR4 does not come in modules larger than 64 GB; larger DDR4 modules exist only as server (registered/load-reduced) parts, so whyWrong says they are not desktop modules.

stem: What is the primary reason that DDR4 RAM is faster than DDR3 RAM?
options: The core speed of the DDR4 RAM chips is faster.
The input/output speed of the DDR4 RAM is faster.
DDR3 RAM is dual-channel and DDR4 RAM is quad-channel.
DDR3 RAM uses 240-pin DIMMs and DDR4 uses 288-pin DIMMs.
explanation: The input/output speed of DDR4 RAM is faster than that of DDR3 RAM (although the latency is higher). The memory core speeds of the two generations are similar, so the gain comes from the faster I/O bus.
whyWrong: The core speed of the RAM chips is similar across DDR3 and DDR4; the I/O speed is what increased.
Both DDR3 and DDR4 can run in dual-channel and other multichannel setups; the channel count is set by the motherboard.
The pin counts are true, but more pins do not by themselves make DDR4 faster.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 4: RAM, Chapter Review question 3

stem: What is the term for the delay in the RAM’s response to a request from the MCC?
explanation: Latency is the term for the delay in the RAM's response to a request from the memory controller chip (MCC). It is often given as a CAS latency (CL) rating, and lower values mean a faster response.
whyWrong: Variance is not a RAM timing term.
MCC gap is not a real memory term.
Fetch interval is not the standard name for the RAM response delay.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 4: RAM, Chapter Review question 4
note: Older book (220-1101/1102), All-in-One 11e Chapter 4: RAM latency. Closest current topic: DDR iterations.

stem: Silas has an AMD-based motherboard with two sticks of DDR3 RAM installed in two of the three RAM slots, for a total of 8 GB of system memory. When he runs CPU-Z to test the system, he notices that the software claims he’s running single-channel memory. What could be the problem? (Select the best answer.)
options: His motherboard only supports single-channel memory.
His motherboard only supports dual-channel memory with DDR2 RAM, not DDR3.
He needs to install a third RAM stick to enable dual-channel memory.
He needs to move one of the installed sticks to a different slot to activate dual-channel memory.
explanation: Motherboards can require you to install RAM in the proper slots to enable dual-channel memory access. In this case, Silas should move one of the installed sticks to a different slot to activate dual-channel memory, and check the motherboard manual for the proper slots.
whyWrong: A board with three RAM slots and two sticks that is reporting single channel more likely has the sticks in the wrong slots.
Dual-channel memory works with DDR3; it is not limited to DDR2.
Dual-channel memory needs a matched pair of sticks, so two sticks are enough.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 4: RAM, Chapter Review question 6

stem: What is the primary reason for using DDR (Double Data Rate) RAM in computer systems?
explanation: DDR RAM transfers data on both the rising and the falling edge of the clock signal. This doubles the transfer rate compared with earlier single data rate memory.
whyWrong: DDR does not increase storage capacity; it is temporary working memory.
Later DDR generations use less voltage, but power efficiency is not the main reason for DDR.
Latency in clock cycles is not lowered by DDR; its main benefit is the higher transfer rate.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 2

stem: Which type of memory module is commonly used in laptops and small form factor computers?
explanation: SODIMM (Small Outline Dual In-line Memory Module) is the memory module used in laptops and small form factor computers. It is about half the length of a desktop DIMM.
whyWrong: A DIMM is the larger memory module used in desktop computers.
RIMM is an old Rambus module type that is no longer used.
MicroDIMM is a very small module that was used only in a few subnotebooks.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 3

stem: What is the primary purpose of ECC (Error-Correcting Code) RAM in a computer system?
options: To provide faster data transfer between the CPU and RAM
To detect and correct memory errors
To increase the storage capacity of the RAM
explanation: ECC RAM uses extra bits to detect and correct memory errors, which improves data integrity. It is used in servers and workstations where a memory error must not corrupt data.
whyWrong: ECC does not make data transfer faster; the error checking can make it slightly slower.
ECC has nothing to do with graphics processing.
ECC does not add capacity; its extra bits are used only for error checking.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 4

stem: What is the primary benefit of using a dual-channel RAM configuration, which utilizes two differently colored memory slots, in a computer system?
explanation: In a dual-channel configuration the memory controller uses two channels at the same time, which gives faster data transfer rates. Matching modules are installed in slots of the same color so that each module is on a different channel.
whyWrong: Dual channel does not change the total capacity of the installed modules.
Dual channel can help integrated graphics a little, but its main benefit is memory bandwidth.
Dual channel does not lower power consumption.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 5

stem: What is the primary advantage of using a quad-channel RAM configuration in a computer system?
explanation: A quad-channel configuration uses four memory channels at the same time. This increases the bandwidth and the data transfer rate between the RAM and the CPU.
whyWrong: Quad channel does not change the total capacity of the installed modules.
Multitasking may benefit from the higher bandwidth, but that is a side effect, not the main advantage.
Memory latency depends on the module speed and timings, not on the number of channels.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 6

stem: DDR RAM is a type of computer memory that offers improved data transfer rates compared to earlier memory technologies. Which of the following options correctly matches the lowest speed for each version of DDR RAM?
options: DDR2 – 400 MHz, DDR3 – 800 MHz, DDR4 – 2,133 MHz
DDR2 – 800 MHz, DDR3 – 1,600 MHz, DDR4 – 3,200 MHz
DDR2 – 1,333 MHz, DDR3 – 1,866 MHz, DDR4 – 2,400 MHz
DDR2 – 2,000 MHz, DDR3 – 2,400 MHz, DDR4 – 3,200 MHz
explanation: The common DDR2 speeds start at 400 MT/s, DDR3 at 800 MT/s, and DDR4 at 2,133 MT/s (often written as MHz). Each generation starts near the top speed of the generation before it.
whyWrong: 800 for DDR2, 1,600 for DDR3, and 3,200 for DDR4 are mid-range or top speeds, not the lowest.
These values are mid-range speeds, not the lowest speed of each generation.
DDR2 never reached 2,000 MHz, and these values are well above the lowest speeds.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 7
note: DDR2 is not in the 220-1201 objectives, but DDR3 and DDR4 are. Old objective 220-1101 3.2 (RAM).

stem: Which of the following options would be the BEST choice for a gaming PC in terms of disk, CPU, and RAM?
options: SSD, Intel Core i5, 8 GB DDR4
HDD, Intel Core i9, 32 GB DDR3
SSD, Intel Core i7, 16 GB DDR4
explanation: An SSD gives fast load times, an Intel Core i7 gives strong processing power, and 16 GB of DDR4 gives enough fast memory for games. Together they are the best balance of the options listed.
whyWrong: An HDD is slow, and a Ryzen 3 with 8 GB of DDR3 is entry-level hardware for gaming.
An SSD and a Core i5 with 8 GB DDR4 are a reasonable start, but the Core i7 and 16 GB are better for gaming.
An HDD slows game loading, and DDR3 is an old, slower memory generation.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.2 question 8
note: 220-1201 has no objective for choosing a full system; tagged with the RAM, storage, and CPU topics. Old objective 220-1101 3.2 (RAM).

stem: How much data can a SATA Revision 3.0 drive transfer per second?
explanation: SATA Revision 3.0 drives can transfer 6 Gb/s, which amounts to about 600 MB/s after encoding. SATA Revision 3.2 reaches 16 Gb/s (1969 MB/s) but requires SATA Express or M.2.
whyWrong: 50 MB/s is a typical write speed for Blu-ray discs and some flash media.
90 MB/s is a typical write speed for an SD card.
1969 MB/s is the speed of SATA Revision 3.2, which needs SATA Express or M.2.
16 Gb/s is the rate of SATA Revision 3.2, not Revision 3.0.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which level of RAID stripes data and parity across three or more disks?
explanation: RAID 5 stripes data and parity across three or more disks. If one disk fails, the array rebuilds its data from the parity information on the other disks.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data only, with no parity, and can use two or more disks.
RAID 1 mirrors data across two disks and uses no parity.
Striping is another name for RAID 0, which has no parity.
RAID 10 stripes across mirrored pairs of disks and uses no parity.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: A customer complains that an important disc is stuck in the system’s Blu-ray drive. What should you recommend to the customer?
options: Get a screwdriver and disassemble the drive.
Use a paper clip to eject the tray.
Dispose of the drive and replace the media.
explanation: Tell the customer to use a paper clip (or a mobile device tray pin) in the drive's small emergency-eject hole to open the Blu-ray tray. This releases the tray manually without opening the computer or harming the disc.
whyWrong: Disassembling the drive is not necessary, and a customer should not be told to do it.
Formatting a rewritable disc would erase the important contents, even if it were possible while the disc is stuck.
Optical drives rarely fail, and a failed drive should be recycled, not thrown away along with the media.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following best describes a specification for accessing storage while using PCI Express?
explanation: Non-Volatile Memory Express (NVMe) is a specification for accessing storage over PCI Express. An M.2 slot on a motherboard taps into the PCIe bus (usually x4) to give NVMe drives far more bandwidth than SATA.
whyWrong: 7200 RPM is a common spindle speed for the platters of a hard disk drive.
Hot-swappable means a drive can be removed and inserted while the system is on.
3.5-inch and 2.5-inch are drive form factors for desktops and laptops, not access specifications.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which RAID level is referred to as striping with double parity and requires a minimum of four or more disks?
explanation: RAID 6 is called striping with double parity and requires a minimum of four disks. Data and two parity blocks are striped across the disks, so the array can rebuild its data even if two disks fail.
whyWrong: RAID 10 is a stripe of mirrors that needs at least four disks but uses mirroring, not parity.
Striping with parity describes RAID 5, which uses single parity and needs at least three disks.
Non-Volatile Memory Express (NVMe) is a specification for accessing storage over PCIe, not a RAID level.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which is the optical standard for high-definition video and can store between 25 GB and 128 GB of data?
explanation: Blu-ray is the optical standard for high-definition video, used for HD movies and console games. A typical Blu-ray disc stores between 25 GB and 128 GB of data.
whyWrong: DVDs hold much more than CDs but far less than Blu-ray discs, and they are not the high-definition standard.
A DVD-5 (single-sided, single-layer) disc stores 4.7 GB.
A DVD-18 (double-sided, dual-layer) disc stores about 17 GB, well below Blu-ray capacities.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 15: Storage Drives, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: You need to describe RAID to a nontechnical customer. Which of the following is the BEST description to use for this customer?
options: RAID stands for redundant array of independent disks.
RAID utilizes multiple disks to increase performance and/or enable protection against data loss.
RAID is a dynamic disk management system.
RAID uses striping to reduce the amount of storage drive write time and utilizes parity bits to reconstruct the data from a failed drive.
explanation: Tell the customer that RAID uses multiple disks to increase performance, protect against data loss, or both. RAID 0, 5, and 10 are often used for read performance, while RAID 1, 5, 6, and 10 protect against data loss; the customer needs to know the benefit, not the jargon.
whyWrong: Spelling out the acronym is technical jargon that does not tell the customer what RAID does.
RAID is not a dynamic disk management system, even though Windows needs dynamic disks for software RAID.
This statement is technical and incomplete: RAID can also mirror, and RAID 0, 1, and 10 use no parity.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 41

stem: You are building a high-performance workstation. You are required to select a boot drive with the highest performance available. Which of the following is the BEST option?
explanation: An NVMe drive, for example an M.2 NVMe SSD, gives the highest performance of the listed options. It transfers data over the PCIe bus, much faster than SATA or a spinning disk.
whyWrong: A 15K rpm HDD is one of the fastest hard drives, but it moves only a fraction of the data an NVMe drive can.
A microSD card is secondary storage for mobile devices and is a poor choice for a boot drive.
A USB flash drive is too slow for a workstation boot drive and is used mainly to test or repair systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 63

stem: You need to install a new M.2 hard drive into a desktop computer. The motherboard has an open M.2 slot that is M-keyed. Which types of M.2 hard drives will you be able to install into that motherboard?
explanation: If the slot is M-keyed, it has a block in the M position. For a drive to fit into that slot, it must have a notch in the M position, which is called being M-keyed. A B+M-keyed drive has notches in both the B and M positions, so it will fit as well.
whyWrong: A drive that is only B-keyed will not fit, because its notch does not line up with the block in the M-keyed connector.
M-key drives fit, but B+M-key drives fit as well, so M-key alone is incomplete.
B+M-key drives fit, but plain M-key drives fit as well, so B+M-key alone is incomplete.
This choice includes B-key drives, which will not fit an M-keyed slot.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 2

stem: A client is looking for a desktop storage technology that provides the fastest possible data transfers. Which technology should you recommend?
explanation: The fastest SSD communications interface is NVMe. Conventional hard drives, whatever their spin rate, will always be slower than SSDs.
whyWrong: SATA is limited to 600 MBps, which is much slower than NVMe.
10,000 rpm is a conventional hard drive spin rate, and spinning drives are slower than SSDs.
15,000 rpm is the fastest common hard drive spin rate, but spinning drives are still slower than SSDs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 5

stem: You are choosing an optical drive format for a client. The client needs to store video files which are about 20 GB in size. Which technology should they use?
explanation: Blu-ray discs have a single-sided, single-layer capacity of 25 GB, which is enough for 20 GB video files. A double-sided, single-layer DVD can store about 9.4 GB, and a double-sided, double-layer DVD can store about 17.1 GB.
whyWrong: A double-sided, double-layer DVD holds about 17.1 GB, which is less than 20 GB.
A double-sided, single-layer DVD-R holds about 9.4 GB.
A double-sided, single-layer DVD+R holds about 9.4 GB.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 6

stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of hot-swappable devices?
options: Power does not need to be turned off before the device is inserted or removed.
The device can be removed with power applied after it is properly stopped in the operating system.
Care must be taken when swapping the device because it can be hot to the touch.
The device can be swapped while still hot, immediately after powering down the system.
explanation: Hot-swappable devices can be removed while the power to the system is still on. Warm-swappable devices need to be stopped in the operating system before being removed.
whyWrong: A device that must be stopped in the operating system before removal is warm-swappable.
The term has nothing to do with how hot the device is to the touch.
Swapping a device after powering down the system is a cold swap, and the term has nothing to do with heat.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 7

stem: You have been asked to install a new hard drive for a client. Which of the following is not a consideration when installing an internal storage device?
options: You should match the form factor of the drive or adapt it to an available drive bay or slot.
You should secure the drive with at least two screws on one side and preferably two on each side.
Due to the high revolutions at which modern hard drives spin, you must secure an external power source because the internal power supplies do not have the capacity.
You need to be sure that the routing of the drive's data cable, if applicable, does not obstruct the engineered flow of air across internal components.
explanation: Today's hard drives, regardless of their rpm, have standard internal power connections. Matching the form factor to a bay, securing the drive with screws, and routing cables so that they do not block airflow are all valid concerns when installing an internal drive.
whyWrong: Matching the drive's form factor to a bay, or adapting it, is a real installation concern.
Securing the drive with screws on both sides is a real installation concern.
Routing the data cable so that it does not block airflow is a real installation concern.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 11

stem: A client just bought a new digital camera for his photography business. Which of the following is specifically designed as an internal storage device for cameras?
explanation: Memory cards such as SD cards were designed for devices such as digital cameras. They fit in a slot inside the camera and can be moved to a card reader to transfer the pictures.
whyWrong: Optical discs are larger and are used mostly with laptops and larger systems, not cameras.
Flash drives connect through USB and are external storage, not internal camera storage.
mSATA is a small SSD form factor for laptops and small systems, not a camera storage card.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 12

stem: You are installing a second hard drive into a desktop computer. The hard drive is an NVMe PCIe card. Which of the following steps will you need to take during installation?
options: Install the hard drive into an open PCIe slot.
Install the hard drive into an open PCIe slot. Connect the NVMe PCIe data cable.
Install the hard drive into an open PCIe slot. Connect the NVMe PCIe power connector.
Install the hard drive into an open PCIe slot. Connect the NVMe PCIe data cable and power connector.
Install the hard drive into an open NVMe slot.
Install the hard drive into an open NVMe slot. Connect the NVMe PCIe data cable.
Install the hard drive into an open NVMe slot. Connect the NVMe PCIe power connector.
Install the hard drive into an open NVMe slot. Connect the NVMe PCIe data cable and power connector.
explanation: NVMe is a communications standard, and there are no NVMe slots. This drive needs to be installed into an open PCIe slot. PCIe drives do not require an additional data cable or power connector, because the slot provides both.
whyWrong: A PCIe card drive gets its data connection through the slot, so no extra data cable is needed.
A PCIe card drive gets its power through the slot, so no extra power connector is needed.
A PCIe card drive gets both data and power through the slot, so no extra cables are needed.
NVMe is a communications standard, and motherboards have no NVMe slots.
There is no NVMe slot, and a PCIe card drive needs no separate data cable.
There is no NVMe slot, and a PCIe card drive needs no separate power connector.
There is no NVMe slot, and a PCIe card drive needs no extra data or power cables.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 13

stem: You are choosing a flash standard for a client. They want the smallest flash cards possible. Which standard should you recommend?
explanation: The smallest of the options is microSD, at 15 mm × 11 mm. SD cards are 32 mm × 24 mm, and miniSD cards measure 21.5 mm × 20 mm.
whyWrong: Standard SD cards are 32 mm × 24 mm, much larger than microSD.
CompactFlash cards are the largest of these, at 36 mm × 43 mm.
MiniSD cards are 21.5 mm × 20 mm, larger than microSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 16

stem: Your goal is to build the fastest computer possible. Which of the following hard drive technologies should you choose for the fastest read performance?
explanation: The fastest drive will be an NVMe drive in an M.2 slot, which uses PCIe lanes with the NVMe protocol. M.2 SATA drives exist, but they are limited to SATA's 600 MBps transfer speed.
whyWrong: An M.2 PCIe label alone does not say the drive uses NVMe; early M.2 PCIe drives used the slower AHCI protocol.
An M.2 SATA drive is limited to the 600 MBps speed of SATA.
NVMe does not run over SATA; SATA drives use AHCI and are limited to 600 MBps.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 17
note: Book explanation says M.2 SATA and M.2 PCIe drives do not exist; M.2 SATA drives do exist and are slower, so the explanation and whyWrong were rewritten. Answer unchanged.

stem: You have been asked to configure a RAID 5 system for a client. Which of the following statements about RAID 5 is true?
options: It provides fault tolerance but no performance improvement.
It provides performance improvement but no fault tolerance.
If multiple drives in the array fail, the data can be saved provided that one drive is still operational.
It requires at least three drives to implement.
explanation: RAID 5 arrays require a minimum of three hard drives to implement. If one drive fails, the data is fine and the system can still function, albeit slowly. If more than one drive fails, the array is lost.
whyWrong: RAID 5 provides a performance improvement as well as fault tolerance.
RAID 5 provides fault tolerance as well as a performance improvement.
RAID 5 survives the failure of only one drive; if more than one fails, the data is lost.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 2: Expansion Cards, Storage Devices, and Power Supplies, Review Questions question 18

stem: Which of the following is a common spindle speed for an HDD?
options: Not applicable. HDDs have no moving parts.
explanation: Common spindle speeds on magnetic hard drives are 5400, 7200, 10,000, and 15,000 RPM. Faster spindle speeds give faster access to data.
whyWrong: 5200 RPM is not a standard spindle speed; the low common speed is 5400 RPM.
9200 RPM is not a standard spindle speed.
HDDs have spinning platters and moving heads; it is SSDs that have no moving parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 1

stem: Which form factor connects directly to a dedicated motherboard socket?
explanation: The M.2 (and mSATA) SSD has a dedicated motherboard socket. The drive plugs straight into the slot with no separate data or power cable.
whyWrong: A 2.5-inch SSD connects through SATA data and power cables, not a dedicated socket.
3.5-inch is a mechanical hard drive size and uses cables.
An eSATA drive is external and connects through an eSATA cable.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 2

stem: Which of the following is an advantage of an NVMe SSD?
options: The ability to hot-swap the drive
explanation: NVMe SSDs offer significantly faster read/write speeds than mechanical hard drives or SATA SSDs. NVMe uses the PCIe bus directly, avoiding the limits of the SATA interface.
whyWrong: NVMe SSDs usually cost more per gigabyte than HDDs or SATA SSDs.
NVMe drives do not offer more capacity than other drive types.
Most NVMe drives are M.2 cards inside the case and are not hot-swappable.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 3

stem: Which of the following is not an SSD form factor?
explanation: 3.5 inch is a form factor for mechanical hard drives, not SSDs. SSDs come as M.2 and mSATA cards and in the 2.5-inch drive size.
whyWrong: M.2 is a common SSD form factor that plugs into a motherboard socket.
2.5-inch is a common SSD form factor that uses SATA cables.
mSATA is a small SSD card form factor used in older laptops.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 4

stem: How do SSDs avoid the need to use moving mechanical parts?
options: By being placed in an external enclosure
explanation: SSDs use flash memory such as NAND in place of the less reliable spinning disks used by mechanical HDDs. With no moving parts, they are faster, quieter, and more resistant to shock.
whyWrong: Magnetic platters are the moving parts of an HDD, which SSDs do not use.
An external enclosure only holds a drive; it does not remove moving parts.
SATA connectors are used by both SSDs and HDDs, so they do not remove moving parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 5

stem: Which standard supports magnetic SATA drives most efficiently?
explanation: The AHCI standard supports magnetic SATA drives efficiently. AHCI (Advanced Host Controller Interface) is the controller mode for SATA drives, while NVMe was designed for flash-based SSDs on the PCIe bus.
whyWrong: CMOS holds firmware settings and is not a drive interface standard.
SATA-IO is the organization that maintains the SATA standard, not a controller standard.
SATA 3.2 is a version of the SATA specification, not the controller standard for drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 9
note: Older book (220-1101/1102), All-in-One 11e Chapter 8: SATA/AHCI. AHCI is not named in 220-1201; mapped to SSD communications interfaces (SATA vs NVMe).

stem: Which RAID standard requires at least four drives?
explanation: RAID 10 requires at least four drives. It stripes data across mirrored pairs, so it combines the speed of RAID 0 with the redundancy of RAID 1.
whyWrong: RAID 1 mirrors data and needs only two drives.
RAID 4 uses a dedicated parity drive and needs at least three drives.
RAID 5 stripes data with parity and needs at least three drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 8: Mass Storage Technologies, Chapter Review question 10

stem: Which configuration requires at least three same-sized volumes?
explanation: RAID 5 requires at least three same-sized volumes. It stripes data and parity across all of the drives, so the array survives the failure of any one drive.
whyWrong: A mirrored set (RAID 1) needs only two volumes.
A spanned volume joins space from drives of any size and needs no third drive.
A striped volume (RAID 0) needs only two volumes.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 9: Implementing Mass Storage, Chapter Review question 8
note: Older book (220-1101/1102), All-in-One 11e Chapter 9: Windows software RAID (dynamic disk volumes). Mapped to RAID drive configurations.

stem: Jason put in a recommendation that his company upgrade the SD cards used in the company smartphones from 32-GB SDHC A1 to 128-GB SDXC A2. What is the advantage of A2 cards over A1 cards?
options: A2 cards offer much greater capacity than A1 cards.
A2 cards offer much faster sustained write speeds than A1 cards.
A2 cards cost a lot less than A1 cards and offer similar performance.
A2 cards sustain faster IOPS than A1 cards.
explanation: A1 and A2 Application Performance Class ratings refer to the IOPS rating of the card, with A2 cards offering better performance than A1. This matters for smartphones with multiple apps running. SDHC and SDXC refer to the capacity of a card's storage.
whyWrong: The capacity difference comes from SDHC versus SDXC, not from the A1 or A2 rating.
Sustained write speed is rated by the speed classes, not the A1 and A2 application classes.
A2 cards usually cost more than A1 cards, not less.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 1

stem: Which optical disc type offers the most capacity writing and rewriting data files?
explanation: BD-RE offers the highest rewritable capacity of the discs mentioned here. A single-layer Blu-ray disc holds 25 GB, far more than a DVD.
whyWrong: DVD-R can be written only once and holds far less than a Blu-ray disc.
DVD+RW DL is rewritable, but a DVD holds much less than a Blu-ray disc.
BD-RW is not the name of the rewritable Blu-ray format; that format is BD-RE.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 10: Essential Peripherals, Chapter Review question 9

stem: What is the primary advantage of installing an M.2 hard drive directly on the motherboard without using cables?
options: Faster data transfer rates through the SATA interface
Increased storage capacity through the NVMe interface
Simpler and more secure connection without cable clutter
Compatibility with legacy systems through the IDE interface
explanation: An M.2 drive plugs directly into a slot on the motherboard and is held by one screw. It needs no data or power cables, which makes the connection simpler and reduces cable clutter in the case.
whyWrong: An M.2 drive can use SATA or NVMe, and the cable-free mounting is not what sets its speed.
The interface does not set storage capacity, which depends on the drive itself.
M.2 drives do not use the legacy IDE interface.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 1

stem: A user wants to replace the existing hard drive with the fastest possible 1 TB drive. Which of the following drive types should the technician recommend as the BEST choice?
explanation: A 1 TB NVMe SSD uses the PCIe bus and is much faster than SATA SSDs and HDDs. It offers the lowest latency and the fastest access times of the options.
whyWrong: eSATA is an interface for external drives, not a type of internal drive.
A USB 3.0 drive is external and slower than an NVMe SSD.
A SATA SSD is limited to about 600 MB/s by the SATA interface, so it is slower than NVMe.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 2
note: The book stem says "1 TB HDD"; changed to "drive" because the answer is an SSD. Old objective 220-1101 3.3 (storage).

stem: Which of the following RPM options is commonly associated with slower rotational speeds for mechanical hard disk drives (HDDs)?
explanation: A 5,400 rpm hard drive spins the slowest of these options, so its data access and transfer are slower. Such drives are common in laptops and low-cost desktops.
whyWrong: 7,200 rpm is the common desktop speed, faster than 5,400 rpm.
10,000 rpm is a fast speed used in high-performance drives.
15,000 rpm is the fastest common speed, used in enterprise drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 3

stem: Which type of storage device is commonly used for portable data storage and transfer?
explanation: USB flash drives are the common device for carrying data between computers because they are small and plug into any USB port. They use solid-state flash memory.
whyWrong: Memory cards are also portable, but they need a card reader and are mainly used in cameras and phones.
An optical drive reads and writes discs; it is not itself a portable storage medium.
A hard disk drive is usually installed inside the computer and is not the common choice for carrying data.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 4

stem: Which storage device uses laser technology to read and write data on optical disks?
explanation: An optical drive uses a laser to read and write data on optical discs such as CDs, DVDs, and Blu-ray discs. The laser reads the pits and lands on the disc surface.
whyWrong: A flash drive stores data in solid-state flash memory, without a laser.
Memory cards such as SD and microSD use flash memory, not a laser.
An SSD stores data in flash memory chips and has no laser or moving parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 6

stem: Which of the following rpm options is commonly associated with faster rotational speeds for mechanical hard disk drives (HDDs)?
explanation: Hard drives that spin at 15,000 rpm have the fastest data access of these options. They are used in enterprise storage, and they make more heat and noise than slower drives.
whyWrong: 5,400 rpm is the slowest common speed, used in laptops and low-cost drives.
7,200 rpm is the common desktop speed, slower than 15,000 rpm.
10,000 rpm is fast but still slower than 15,000 rpm.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 8

stem: You have three hard drives, sized 500 GB, 1 TB, and 2 TB. Which RAID configuration would provide both data redundancy and increased storage capacity?
explanation: RAID 5 needs at least three drives and stripes data with parity across them. It survives the failure of one drive and gives more capacity than a single drive.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data with no redundancy, so one drive failure loses all data.
RAID 1 mirrors two drives, so it gives redundancy but no extra capacity.
RAID 10 needs at least four drives, and only three are available.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 9

stem: You have four hard drives, sized 2 TB, 2 TB, 4 TB, and 4 TB. Which RAID configuration uses a minimum of four drives and would provide both data redundancy and increased storage capacity? (Choose two)
explanation: RAID 6 needs at least four drives and uses two parity blocks, so it survives two drive failures. RAID 10 also needs at least four drives and combines mirroring with striping, so it gives both redundancy and more capacity than a single drive.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data with no redundancy, so one drive failure loses all data.
RAID 5 gives redundancy but needs a minimum of only three drives, not four.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 11

stem: You have two hard drives of different sizes, a 1 TB drive and a 500 GB drive. Which RAID configuration would be most suitable for mirroring the data between the drives?
explanation: RAID 1 (mirroring) writes the same data to both drives, so if one fails the other keeps working. With drives of different sizes, the mirror is limited to the size of the smaller drive.
whyWrong: RAID 0 (striping) does not provide any redundancy.
RAID 5 needs a minimum of three drives.
RAID 10 needs a minimum of four drives.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 12

stem: Which storage device is commonly used in digital cameras and smartphones for expanding storage capacity?
explanation: Memory cards such as SD and microSD cards are used in digital cameras and smartphones to add storage. They are small and fit in the card slot of the device.
whyWrong: Cameras and phones have no USB-A port for a flash drive; they use memory cards.
Optical drives are not used in cameras or smartphones.
SSDs are used in computers, not as expansion storage for cameras or phones.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 13

stem: An IT support technician is upgrading their laptop to provide remote administration and run several programs at one time. The read-write speed needs to be the fastest possible. Which of the following options would fulfill their criteria?
explanation: An M.2 NVMe SSD connects over PCIe and gives the fastest read and write speeds of these laptop options. It is much faster than SATA-based SSDs and any spinning drive.
whyWrong: A SAS HDD is a spinning server drive, much slower than an SSD and not used in laptops.
A 40 GB IDE HDD is a slow, small legacy drive.
An mSATA SSD uses the SATA interface, so it is slower than an NVMe SSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 14

stem: What is a key difference between installing a 2.5” SSD and a 3.5” SSD on a desktop computer?
explanation: The key difference between 2.5-inch and 3.5-inch drives is their physical form factor and size. A 2.5-inch drive fits laptops and small desktops (or a 3.5-inch bay with an adapter), while a 3.5-inch drive needs a full desktop bay.
whyWrong: Both sizes use the same SATA power connector, so power requirements are not the key difference.
Transfer speed depends on the interface and the flash memory, not on the physical size.
Drive bay fit follows from the size; it is a result of the form factor, not the key difference itself.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.3 question 15

stem: What type of disk infrastructure is typically used in a degraded state?
explanation: A RAID array with redundancy can keep running in a degraded state after a disk fails. It runs with reduced redundancy and performance until the failed disk is replaced and the array is rebuilt.
whyWrong: A single SATA disk has no redundancy, so when it fails, its data is gone.
A single SSD has no redundancy and cannot run in a degraded state.
A single external USB disk has no redundancy and cannot run in a degraded state.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.4 question 21
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.4 (motherboards, CPUs, add-on cards).

stem: A customer has called an IT support company to provide a storage solution. The customer has purchased three 20-TB hard drives and the solution must provide fast read access and redundancy. Which of the following solutions would be the BEST to implement?
explanation: RAID 5 uses a minimum of three disks, gives fast read speeds, and stripes parity across the disks. With RAID 5, you can lose one disk and still keep your data.
whyWrong: RAID 0 stripes data for speed but has no fault tolerance, so one failed disk loses all the data.
RAID 1 mirrors two disks for redundancy but would leave the third disk unused and does not give the read speed of striping across three disks.
RAID 6 needs a minimum of four disks, and the customer has only three.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.3 question 1
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.3 (storage); tagged to current 3.4 drive configurations.

stem: Which of the following is true about the M.2 form factor?
options: M.2 supports only the SATA interface
M.2 is exclusively used for graphics cards
M.2 allows faster data transfer rates compared to traditional hard drives
M.2 cannot be used as a boot device
explanation: M.2 is a form factor that is commonly used for solid-state drives (SSDs), and it allows much faster data transfer than traditional hard drives. M.2 drives can use the SATA or the PCIe (NVMe) interface.
whyWrong: M.2 supports both the SATA and the PCIe interfaces, not only SATA.
M.2 is used mostly for SSDs and wireless cards, while graphics cards use full-size PCIe slots.
An M.2 drive can be used as a boot device.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 1
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is a characteristic of RAID 5?
options: Requires a minimum of three drives
Provides the highest level of fault tolerance
Offers increased read performance compared to RAID 0
explanation: RAID 5 requires a minimum of three drives. It stripes data and parity across all the drives, so the array keeps working if one drive fails.
whyWrong: RAID 5 survives only one drive failure; RAID 6, with dual parity, gives higher fault tolerance.
RAID 0 stripes data with no parity, so RAID 5 does not read faster than RAID 0.
RAID 5 spreads parity across all drives instead of using a dedicated parity drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 2
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which of the following flash memory card formats is commonly used in digital cameras?
explanation: Secure Digital (SD) cards are the flash memory card format most commonly used in digital cameras. They are widely adopted and come in many capacities for storing photos and videos.
whyWrong: CompactFlash (CF) was popular in the past, but SD cards have largely replaced it.
Memory Stick (MS) was used mainly in Sony devices.
eXtreme Digital (xD) cards are uncommon and were used in older Olympus and Fujifilm cameras.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 3
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: Which motherboard form factor measures 12 inches × 9.6 inches (305 mm × 244 mm)?
explanation: ATX boards measure 12 × 9.6 inches (305 × 244 mm). ATX is the standard full-size form factor for desktop motherboards.
whyWrong: microATX boards are square and measure 9.6 × 9.6 inches (244 × 244 mm).
SATA is a storage drive interface and the port that connects drives to the motherboard, not a form factor.
mITX (Mini-ITX) boards are square and measure 6.7 × 6.7 inches (170 × 170 mm).
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Which component supplies power to the CMOS when a computer is off?
explanation: The lithium battery (CMOS battery) on the motherboard supplies power to the CMOS when the computer is off. The CMOS is volatile and would otherwise lose the stored BIOS/UEFI settings, including the date and time.
whyWrong: POST (power-on self-test) is the set of hardware checks the firmware runs at startup, not a power source.
The power supply provides no power to the CMOS when the computer is unplugged.
The BIOS/UEFI is the firmware whose settings the CMOS stores; it does not supply power.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: To implement a Secure Boot process, which device should be listed first in the Boot Device Priority screen?
explanation: To make sure other users cannot boot the computer from removable media, set the hard drive as the first device in the Boot Device Priority screen. Secure Boot and a BIOS/UEFI password add further protection.
whyWrong: Booting from the network first would let the computer load an operating system from a network server.
Putting the optical drive first would let anyone boot the computer from a disc.
Putting USB first would let anyone boot the computer from a flash drive.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: Which of the following connectors might you use to power a video card?
explanation: A video card is normally powered by a 6-pin or 8-pin PCIe power connector; newer high-end cards use the 16-pin 12VHPWR connector. Lower-power cards take all their power from the PCIe slot.
whyWrong: The 24-pin connector is the main power connection from the power supply to the motherboard.
SATA power connectors feed storage drives, fans, and other secondary devices.
The 3.5 mm TRS connector is an audio connection, not a power connector.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which of the following is a chip that stores encryption keys?
explanation: A Trusted Platform Module (TPM) is a chip on most motherboards that stores encryption keys for drive encryption. It is enabled in the BIOS/UEFI.
whyWrong: Intel VT is a firmware feature that supports virtualization software such as Hyper-V and VMware.
Secure Boot blocks tampered boot loaders, such as those changed by rootkits, from launching.
Firmware such as the BIOS/UEFI is the software in the motherboard's chip, and it should be updated periodically.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following BIOS/UEFI settings are used to prevent USB drop attacks?
explanation: Configure USB permissions in the BIOS/UEFI to prevent USB drop attacks, in which an attacker leaves an infected USB drive where someone will plug it in. Disabling USB ports in the firmware stops the drive from being used at all.
whyWrong: A boot password keeps people from changing the settings, but it does not control USB ports itself.
The BIOS time/date settings set the system clock and do not stop USB drives from being used.
Storage area network (SAN) settings have no relationship to USB devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: What do the POWER LED, POWER SW, and HDD LED plugs connect to on the motherboard?
explanation: The case's power LED, power switch, and storage drive LED cables plug into headers on the motherboard, specifically the front panel header. The motherboard manual shows which pin each cable uses.
whyWrong: The 7-pin SATA port connects the data cable of a storage drive.
PCIe slots hold expansion cards such as video, sound, and network cards.
The 24-pin ATX port takes the main power connection from the power supply.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: Which of the following is a removable unit that runs on its own and includes a cryptoprocessor that generates, stores, and manages digital keys?
explanation: A hardware security module (HSM) is a removable unit that runs on its own. It includes a cryptoprocessor that generates, stores, and manages digital keys and performs fast cryptographic operations.
whyWrong: A storage area network (SAN) is a dedicated high-speed network that lets servers use pooled storage like local disks.
POST (power-on self-test) is the set of diagnostic tests the firmware runs on critical hardware at startup.
A TPM is a chip built into the motherboard, not a removable unit.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 16: Motherboards and Add-on Cards, Cram Quiz question 8

stem: What does multithreading do?
options: It gives you multiple cores within the CPU.
It enables four simultaneous threads to be processed by one CPU core.
It enables two simultaneous threads to be processed by one CPU core.
It provides a high-speed connection from the CPU to RAM.
explanation: Multithreading lets the operating system send two simultaneous threads to a single CPU core. The OS sees each core as two virtual (logical) processors.
whyWrong: Multiple physical cores in one CPU package is multicore technology, not multithreading.
Multithreading such as Intel Hyper-Threading runs two threads per core, not four.
A high-speed link from the CPU to RAM, such as AMD's HyperTransport, is a bus technology, not multithreading.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: What seals the tiny gaps between the CPU cap and the heat sink?
explanation: Thermal paste seals the small gaps between the CPU and the heat sink so that heat moves well into the heat sink. It is also called thermal compound or thermal gel.
whyWrong: Grape jelly is food and would damage a CPU; the thermal material is only sometimes nicknamed thermal jelly.
Plumber's putty is a sealant for plumbing fixtures and does not conduct heat well.
Never use petroleum-based products such as 3-in-1 oil inside a computer, because the oils damage components over time.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following can be defined as the amount of heat generated by the CPU, which the cooling system is required to dissipate?
explanation: TDP (thermal design power) is the amount of heat a CPU generates that the cooling system must dissipate. It tells you how strong a heat sink and fan, or liquid cooler, the CPU needs.
whyWrong: A GPU is a graphics processing unit, which can be built into some CPUs; it is not a heat measurement.
PSU stands for power supply unit, the part that converts AC power for the computer.
140 watts is a possible TDP rating, but it is a value, not the definition of TDP.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: When you’re deciding on a CPU for use with a specific motherboard, what does it need to be compatible with? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: The CPU must be compatible with the socket on the motherboard. It must also be compatible with the motherboard's chipset, which may need a BIOS/UEFI update to support newer CPUs.
whyWrong: The case affects the choice of motherboard form factor, but not the choice of CPU.
PCIe slots do not connect directly to the CPU socket choice, so they do not decide CPU compatibility.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: Which kind of socket incorporates “lands” to ensure connectivity to a CPU?
explanation: An LGA (land grid array) socket uses pins in the socket that touch flat "lands" on the bottom of the CPU. Intel CPUs and newer AMD AM5 CPUs use LGA sockets.
whyWrong: A PGA (pin grid array) socket has pinholes that take pins on the CPU, not lands.
The chipset is the set of controller chips on the motherboard, not a type of socket.
Copper is the metal used in CPU pins and contacts, not a socket type.
AM4 is a PGA socket for older AMD Ryzen CPUs, so it uses pins, not lands.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: Which of the following enables the user to increase the base clock within the BIOS, thereby increasing the clock speed of the CPU?
explanation: Overclocking means raising the base clock (or multiplier) in the BIOS/UEFI so that the CPU runs at a higher clock speed than its rating. It produces more heat, so it needs better cooling.
whyWrong: L3 cache is the largest and slowest of the three CPU cache levels; it holds data, not clock settings.
An integrated GPU is a video adapter built into the CPU or motherboard.
A heat sink dissipates heat from the CPU and does not change its clock speed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: Which of the following would you use if you needed a typical CPU for a PC that can access 16 GB of RAM?
explanation: You would want an x86-64 (x64) CPU, the typical CPU architecture for a PC. This 64-bit architecture goes beyond the 32-bit limit of 4 GB of RAM and can address far more memory.
whyWrong: ARM-based CPUs are used more often in smartphones, tablets, and other mobile devices than in typical PCs.
RISC (reduced instruction set computing) is the design approach used in ARM CPUs, not a typical PC CPU.
x86 is the older 32-bit PC architecture, which cannot use more than 4 GB of RAM.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: A technician needs to install a new server system in a data center that can run more than one physical CPU at a time. Which configuration will support this requirement?
explanation: Some computers, such as servers, have multisocket motherboards that hold more than one physical CPU at the same time. Each of those CPUs can also be multicore and multithreaded.
whyWrong: A single-core CPU has one processing core, and it says nothing about running more than one physical CPU.
Multicore means several cores inside one physical CPU package, not several CPUs.
Multithreading runs two threads on each core of one CPU; it does not add physical CPUs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 17: CPUs, Cram Quiz question 8

stem: Which of the following components can be considered the “brains” of a computer?
explanation: The central processing unit (CPU), or processor, is often called the brains of the computer. It performs the bulk of the calculations for the system.
whyWrong: RAM stores data over the short term and loses its contents when the computer shuts down.
A storage drive keeps data over the long term, even when the computer is shut down.
The motherboard is the central connecting point for the CPU, RAM, storage, and other components.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 1

stem: You are attempting to load an operating system from a USB flash drive at computer startup. Which of the following settings should you modify in the UEFI/BIOS?
explanation: Most computers' BIOS/UEFI boots from the storage drive first. To boot from a USB flash drive or other removable media, change the boot sequence (boot order or boot priority) so that the removable media comes first.
whyWrong: A BIOS password protects the firmware settings but does not change which device the computer boots from.
TPM handles drive encryption and has no bearing on the boot sequence.
TPM handles drive encryption, so disabling it does not make the computer boot from USB.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 2

stem: You are attempting to install Hyper-V on a Windows computer. However, you receive an error saying that the software cannot be installed. Which of the following CPU characteristics should be checked?
explanation: Check whether the CPU's virtualization support is enabled in the UEFI/BIOS. If it is not, Windows will not install Hyper-V and may show an error or gray out the option in Windows Features.
whyWrong: The number of cores does not cause the Hyper-V installation error.
Hyper-Threading does not decide whether Hyper-V can be installed.
The cache size does not cause an error when you install Hyper-V.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 68

stem: You need to run a diagnostic program by booting to a USB flash drive on a laptop running Windows. You modify the boot order in the UEFI/BIOS and set it to the flash drive first. However, the laptop still boots into Windows. What do you need to adjust to boot to the USB flash drive?
explanation: Secure Boot works with operating systems such as Windows to make sure that only a trusted, signed operating system boots, and it can block booting from external media such as USB sticks. To boot from the flash drive, you most likely need to disable Secure Boot as well as change the boot order.
whyWrong: TPM (Trusted Platform Module) encrypts the storage drive and does not control which device boots.
You already know the UEFI/BIOS password, since you changed the boot order, and it does not block booting from USB.
Virtualization support lets the CPU run virtual machine software and has no effect on the boot device.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 80

stem: Which computer component contains all the circuitry necessary for other components or devices to communicate with one another?
explanation: The spine of the computer is the system board, otherwise known as the motherboard. All other computer components plug into the motherboard. On the motherboard, you will find the CPU, underlying circuitry, expansion slots, video components, RAM slots, and various other chips.
whyWrong: The CPU processes instructions, but it relies on the motherboard's circuitry to reach the other components.
RAM holds data and programs while they run; it does not connect the other devices to each other.
An expansion bus is only one part of the motherboard's circuitry, used to connect add-on cards.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 1

stem: A client wants you to build a new PC for her, with a smaller case and lower power requirements. When selecting a motherboard, which form factor should you choose for a smaller size and lower power consumption?
explanation: The ITX motherboard family consists of smaller boards that fit in standard or miniature cases and use less power than their larger counterparts. ATX boards are the standard size in today's desktops.
whyWrong: ATX is the standard full-size form factor, so it is larger than ITX and uses more power.
AT is a legacy form factor that was even bigger than ATX.
DTX is not a motherboard form factor covered by the exam objectives.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 4
note: The book says no DTX boards exist; whyWrong only says DTX is not an exam form factor.

stem: A motherboard failed on your desktop PC, which has an Intel Core i5-13600K processor. When you're looking for a replacement motherboard, which CPU socket does it need to have?
explanation: The Core i5-13600K is a Raptor Lake (13th generation) processor, which uses the LGA 1700 socket. A replacement motherboard must have the socket that matches the CPU, or the processor will not fit.
whyWrong: LGA 1366 is a much older socket for early Core i7 processors.
LGA 1150 is an older socket for 4th and 5th generation Intel Core processors.
LGA 1200 is the socket for 10th and 11th generation Intel Core processors.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 5

stem: You have just replaced a processor in a computer and now need to add a cooling mechanism. What should you use to attach the cooling system to the processor?
explanation: Thermal paste and thermal pads are used to attach heat sinks and fans to processors. A heat sink usually gets attached to the processor using thermal paste, and then the fan is attached to the heat sink.
whyWrong: The heat sink is the cooling device itself; it needs thermal paste to make good contact with the processor.
A fan is part of the cooling system and is usually attached to the heat sink, not directly to the processor.
Superglue does not transfer heat properly and would likely melt and cause processor failure.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 6

stem: A technician asks you how to get a computer's processor to run faster than it currently does. What is he trying to achieve?
explanation: Overclocking is when someone sets the speed of the processor to run faster than it was rated for. While overclocking can make a computer faster, it can also cause the processor to produce more heat.
whyWrong: Hyperthreading allows a processor core to handle multiple processes at the same time.
Virtualization creates multiple virtual machines on one computer; it does not raise the processor's speed.
Multicore means the processor has more than one core, which is a design feature, not a configurable speed option.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 7

stem: You are assembling a new computer and are looking at new cooling systems. Which of the following cooling systems requires the use of a pump?
explanation: Liquid cooling systems require a reservoir of liquid and a pump to circulate the liquid. If such a system malfunctions, it could cause a mess inside the computer.
whyWrong: Thermal paste is used to attach a heat sink to a processor and has no moving parts.
A heat sink is a passive metal device that does not use a pump.
A heat sink and fan cools with moving air, not with pumped liquid.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 8

stem: Which of the following types of processors will likely generally be preferred for mobile devices?
explanation: ARM processors usually are smaller and generate less heat than x64/x86 CISC processors. Therefore, they are better options for mobile devices.
whyWrong: x64 processors are CISC designs that usually produce more heat and use more power than ARM processors.
x86 processors are CISC designs that usually produce more heat and use more power than ARM processors.
LGA is a type of CPU socket, not a type of processor.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 9

stem: You press the front power button on a computer and the system boots. Later, you press it briefly and the system hibernates. When you press it again, the system resumes. You press and hold the button and the system shuts down. What is this feature called?
explanation: Soft power is the feature whereby the front power button acts as a relay to initiate various system power changes, depending on the duration that the button is held. The button connects to a front panel header on the motherboard rather than switching the power supply directly.
whyWrong: Programmable power is not a recognized power feature name.
Relay power is not a valid power feature name.
Hot power is not a valid power feature name.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 10

stem: You are installing a new computer, and the user wants to use virtualization. Which two hardware components need to support virtual technology for this to work properly? (Choose two.)
explanation: For virtualization to work, both the CPU and the BIOS need to support it, and the operating system does as well. Virtualization support may need to be manually enabled in the BIOS.
whyWrong: RAM does not need any special support for virtualization, although a host needs enough of it.
Apart from its BIOS, the motherboard does not need to support virtualization.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 1: Motherboards, Processors, and Memory, Review Questions question 12

stem: You find out that a disgruntled ex-employee's computer has a boot password that must be entered before the operating system is ever loaded.
