1,000 W is meant for high-end gaming or workstation systems with powerful graphics cards.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.5 question 8

stem: Where would you go in Windows to enable printer sharing?
explanation: The Network and Sharing Center (its advanced sharing settings) is where file and printer sharing is turned on in Windows. After that, you share the specific printer in its printer properties.
whyWrong: Network Connections shows a system's Ethernet and Wi-Fi adapters, not sharing settings.
Windows printer sharing is set in Windows, not on the printer's operator control panel.
Bonjour is an Apple service that discovers devices on the LAN automatically; it does not turn on Windows sharing.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: Your printer supports printing to both sides of a piece of paper. What should you enable in the Printing preferences to print on both sides?
explanation: Duplexing means printing on both sides of the paper. A printer with a duplexing unit turns the page over automatically when duplex is enabled in Printing preferences.
whyWrong: Collating prints each copy of a document in page order instead of all copies of one page at a time.
Orientation sets whether the page prints in portrait (vertical) or landscape (horizontal).
Quality sets the clarity of the print, usually measured in dots per inch (DPI).
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: Which of the following address printer data privacy concerns? (Select the two best answers.)
options: Implementing user authentication on the device
explanation: User authentication on the printer or print server (a PIN or password) keeps others from collecting or viewing print jobs. Clearing the printer's cache removes stored copies of documents that someone could recover.
whyWrong: PCL (Printer Control Language) is a printer driver type for typical office printing, not a privacy control.
AirPrint is an Apple technology that finds printers and their drivers automatically; it does not protect print data.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: When you are finished installing a new printer and print drivers, what should you do? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: After the printer is connected and its drivers are installed, calibrate the printer if needed and print a test page. Also consider updating the printer's firmware.
whyWrong: Installing the print drivers is part of the installation, which the question says is already finished.
Checking compatibility with the operating system and applications is done before the installation starts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: A technician is setting up a printer for a customer who prints professional graphics and presentations. Which print driver should be installed?
explanation: PostScript drivers are made for professional graphics and presentations because they describe pages precisely and look the same on any PostScript printer. PCL drivers are more common and are used for typical office printing.
whyWrong: PCL is the more common driver for typical office printing, not for professional graphics.
ADF stands for automatic document feeder, which feeds multipage documents into a scanner, copier, or fax.
SMB (Server Message Block) is a network file sharing protocol, not a print driver.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A large company with several printers and Windows print servers located throughout the enterprise hires you to implement printer security measures. What industry-standard recommendations should you consider? (Select all that apply.)
options: Turn off all file and printer sharing
explanation: Printer security can be implemented through user authentication and policies, along with badging and secured prints. Audit logs show what was printed, where it was printed, and who printed it.
whyWrong: Turning off all file and printer sharing would stop the users of a large company from reaching its shared printers.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 19: Multifunction Devices/Printers, Cram Quiz question 6

stem: You are configuring a new laser printer. Which laser printer configuration setting do you need to change if users want to have both letter-sized paper and legal-sized paper automatically available?
explanation: Multiple paper trays let a laser printer supply different paper sizes automatically. To set which tray holds which type of paper, change the tray settings configuration options.
whyWrong: Duplex is the setting for two-sided printing.
Orientation chooses portrait or landscape.
Quality affects options such as print resolution.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 10

stem: A workgroup of five PCs uses a shared printer. A customer is not able to print to the printer but can access shares on another PC used for common files. The printer appears to be powered on. Which of the following would be the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: The PC with the connected printer is off the network.
The printer needs to be restarted.
The printer is low on toner.
explanation: The PC that the shared printer is connected to is most likely off the network. The printer seems to be attached to that PC (for example by USB) and shared from it, and because the user can reach shares on other PCs, the user's own computer works on the network.
whyWrong: Restarting the printer fixes some problems, but the printer is on and would most likely return to the same state.
Low toner does not stop the printer from being reached; it would only show a warning message.
Corrupted drivers usually still let the printer be reached, though print jobs may come out garbled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 57

stem: You just set up a printer in the company training room. The trainer wants to be able to print multiple copies of the training documentation for class, and to comply with the company’s new green policy, the trainer needs to conserve paper by printing on both sides of the documents. To comply with the policy, which feature should they be primarily concerned about?
explanation: The trainer needs duplexing, which means printing on both sides of the paper. Many organizations require it in their green policies, but most printers are not set to duplex by default.
whyWrong: Orientation sets whether the page prints in portrait (vertical) or landscape (horizontal).
Print quality is the print resolution, measured in dots per inch (DPI).
Sharing lets users on other computers send jobs to the printer, but it does not save paper.
An automatic document feeder (ADF) feeds multipage originals for scanning, copying, and faxing; it does not print on both sides.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 59

stem: A user has a printer attached to their computer. They configured the printer so other users on the network can print to it. What does that make their computer?
explanation: If a user shares their printer on a network, their computer becomes a print server. The shared printer itself is the printer share.
whyWrong: The printer share is the shared printer itself, not the computer that shares it.
Other users might scan through a network scan service, but sharing a printer does not make the computer one.
An automatic document feeder (ADF) is a physical paper feature of some MFDs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 1

stem: Which of the following is not an advantage of a Universal Serial Bus (USB) printer interface?
options: It has a higher transfer rate than a serial connection.
It has a higher transfer rate than a parallel connection.
It allows the printer to communicate with networks, servers, and workstations.
explanation: The rate of transfer and the ability to recognize new devices automatically are two of the major advantages that make USB the most popular printer interface. However, it is the network printer interface that allows the printer to communicate with networks, servers, and workstations.
whyWrong: USB is faster than a serial connection, so this is an advantage of USB.
USB is faster than a parallel connection, so this is an advantage of USB.
USB recognizes new devices automatically, so this is an advantage of USB.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 3

stem: Which of the following is a type of device that lets users scan in 10-page double-sided documents all at once?
explanation: An automatic document feeder (ADF) allows users to put multiple pieces of paper into it and scan them all as one job. A flatbed scanner allows only one piece of paper at a time.
whyWrong: SMB is used with network scan services to scan to a shared folder.
An MFD is a multifunction printer/scanner device as a whole, not the part that feeds pages.
A flatbed scanner scans only one sheet at a time.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 6

stem: Recently, employees have printed off unauthorized materials which may contain prohibited hate speech. Which of the following can be used to see which users printed specific jobs?
explanation: Audit logs track print jobs and the users who printed them. They let an administrator see which user printed a specific job.
whyWrong: Badging is a way to authenticate at the printer by swiping an employee badge; it does not report past jobs.
User authentication requires a user to log in to the printer, but it does not by itself show who printed past jobs.
Secured prints hold a job until the user authenticates at the printer; they do not report past jobs.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 7

stem: The network administrator has set up security on office MFDs that requires users to authenticate before printing. Which of the following are valid methods for users to authenticate to the MFD? (Choose two.)
options: Type their username and password on the MFD's touchscreen.
Use their company ID for badging.
explanation: Two ways for users to authenticate are user authentication, which requires typing in the username and password, and badging, which requires the MFD to have a badge scanner. Audit logs may also be used to see who has used the MFD, but they do not authenticate users.
whyWrong: Printers have no authentication logs, and audit logs only record who used the device.
Secured print holds print jobs until they are released; it is not itself a way to authenticate.
SMB is a file sharing protocol that MFDs use to send scans to a shared folder.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 10

stem: Which of the following are possible interfaces for printers? (Choose three.)
explanation: Printers can communicate via parallel, serial, USB, wireless, and network (Ethernet) connections. USB, Ethernet, and wireless are the connection types named in the current objectives.
whyWrong: SATA connects storage devices such as hard drives and optical drives to a host bus adapter, not printers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 13

stem: Which of the following most accurately describes how to obtain a firmware upgrade for your laser printer?
options: Download the firmware upgrade for free from the manufacturer's website.
Pay to download the firmware upgrade from the manufacturer's website.
Have a certified laser printer technician come to your site and install a new firmware chip.
Contact the manufacturer of the printer, and they will send you the firmware upgrade on an SSD.
explanation: Firmware upgrades for laser printers are downloaded for free from the manufacturer's website. A technician does not need to install a new chip, because firmware is upgraded via software.
whyWrong: Manufacturers provide printer firmware upgrades free of charge.
Firmware is upgraded through software, so no new chip needs to be installed.
The manufacturer will refer you to its website to download the upgrade rather than ship it on an SSD.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 20

stem: A printer is printing unusually large margins on documents that are sent to it. You suspect that the paper size is set incorrectly. Where should you go to change this?
options: Paper selection switch on the printer
explanation: Printing preferences sets configuration options such as color vs. black and white, paper size, and page orientation. A wrong paper size there makes the page layout and margins come out wrong.
whyWrong: The print spooler is where print jobs are held for printing, not where paper size is set.
Printers do not have a paper selection switch for setting the paper size.
The print queue is the list of print jobs waiting to be printed.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 13: Mobile Device, Display, and Printer Troubleshooting, Review Questions question 2

stem: Which one of the following port types do most printers support?
explanation: Almost all non-networked printers connect through USB ports. Many printers also offer Ethernet or wireless connections.
whyWrong: PS/2 ports are for keyboards and mice, not printers.
Infrared printing was rare and has disappeared.
RS-232 serial is a legacy connection that modern printers rarely support.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 7

stem: A system administrator has installed a new laser printer for the customer service team. After installation, they attempt to print a test page, but it fails to print. What should they do FIRST?
options: Download the driver from the manufacturer’s website
explanation: When a new printer fails to print a test page from the computer, the driver is a likely cause: the installation media may not have a driver for the operating system. The administrator should FIRST download the current driver from the manufacturer's website.
whyWrong: Calibration fixes color and alignment quality; it does not fix a printer that prints nothing.
Rebooting does not help when the computer has no correct driver for the printer.
A new printer comes with a toner cartridge, and empty toner would still let a page come out.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 2: Networking, Objective 2.4 question 12
note: Old 220-1101 2.4 (networked hosts) set; the content matches 220-1201 3.7 (printer drivers).

stem: When using the scan-to-email feature on a multifunction device (MFD), what configuration is required to send the scanned document as an email attachment?
options: Configuring the MFD with the IP address of an SMTP server
Enabling Wi-Fi connectivity on the MFD
Installing email client software on the MFD
Connecting the MFD to a network printer
explanation: Scan to email needs the MFD configured with the address of an SMTP server. The SMTP server accepts the scanned document as an attachment and delivers the email, and it may require authentication.
whyWrong: Wi-Fi gives the MFD a network connection but does not tell it how to send email.
An MFD does not run an email client; it sends mail through an SMTP server.
Connecting to a network printer has nothing to do with sending scans by email.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 4

stem: What is the purpose of a print server?
options: To manage the printing process and control print jobs
To provide network connectivity for printers
To share printers and enable print jobs from multiple computers
To store and manage printer drivers
explanation: A print server shares printers so that many computers can send print jobs to them. It also holds the print queues and can give the printer drivers to the client computers.
whyWrong: A print server does queue and control jobs, but it does this as part of its main purpose: sharing printers.
Printers get network connectivity from their own network interface, not from a print server.
A print server can hold drivers for clients, but that is not its main purpose.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 5
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.6 (printers and MFDs).

stem: You notice that unauthorized individuals are using the printer without permission. This has resulted in the printer paper budget doubling in size. What should be implemented to address this security concern and reduce the paper budget?
explanation: User authentication and access control make sure only authorized people can print. This can use login credentials, PINs, or badges at the printer, and it lets the audit logs show who printed what.
whyWrong: Maintenance keeps the printer working but does not stop unauthorized use.
A driver update does not control who is allowed to print.
Network troubleshooting fixes connection faults, not unauthorized printing.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 6

stem: You have a printer with two paper trays – the top tray contains paper, and the bottom tray contains labels. You notice that when printing, the documents are printed on labels instead of paper. What could be the issue? (Choose two)
options: The top paper tray has run out of paper
The paper tray selection is wrong
The printer driver needs to be updated
The ink or toner is low
explanation: If the top tray runs out of paper, the printer may switch to the next tray, which holds labels. A wrong tray selection in the printer settings or the print dialog also sends the job to the label tray.
whyWrong: A driver update does not change which tray the printer uses.
Low ink or toner causes faded prints, not printing on the wrong media.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 12
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.6 (printers and MFDs).

stem: When using the scan-to-folder feature on a multifunction device (MFD), what configuration is required to save the scanned document as a file on a shared network folder?
options: Configuring the MFD with the path to a suitably configured file server and shared folder
Enabling Bluetooth connectivity on the MFD
Installing file compression software on the MFD
Connecting the MFD to a USB storage device
explanation: Scan to folder uses SMB, so the MFD must be set up with the network path to a correctly configured file server and shared folder. Each user also needs write permission on the shared folder.
whyWrong: Bluetooth is not used to save scans to a network folder.
Compression software has nothing to do with saving scans to a shared folder.
A USB storage device saves scans locally, not to a shared network folder.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 14

stem: When using the scan-to-cloud feature on a multifunction device (MFD), what does it mean to scan to the cloud?
options: Uploading the scan as a file to a document storage and sharing account in the cloud
Sending the scan as an email attachment to a cloud service provider
Printing the scan directly from the MFD to a cloud-based printer
Saving the scan on a local network server accessible from the cloud
explanation: Scan to cloud uploads the scanned document as a file to a cloud storage and sharing account, such as OneDrive or Dropbox. The MFD must be set up with the account details.
whyWrong: Sending the scan as an attachment is scan to email, not scan to cloud.
Printing to a cloud printer is not part of scanning.
Saving to a local server is scan to folder (SMB), not scan to cloud.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 15

stem: You are experiencing issues where many print jobs are not getting picked up from the printer’s paper trays. What can be implemented to prevent this issue?
options: Enable printing only when authorized users insert a PIN
Clearing the print queue and restarting the printer
Replacing the printer’s ink or toner cartridges
explanation: Secured printing holds each job until the user enters a PIN at the printer. Because the user must be at the printer, jobs are not printed and then forgotten in the tray.
whyWrong: A driver update does not stop users from leaving their prints in the tray.
Clearing the queue deletes jobs and does not stop the problem from happening again.
Ink or toner has nothing to do with jobs that are left in the tray.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 16

stem: When connecting a USB printer to a computer running Windows 10, what is the most important step to ensure proper functionality?
options: Installing the latest printer driver compatible with Windows 10
Ensuring the USB cable is securely connected to both the printer and the computer
Configuring the printer settings to match the desired paper size
explanation: The printer driver lets the operating system send print commands to the printer. Installing the latest driver made for Windows 10 is the most important step for the printer to work properly.
whyWrong: Selecting the model matters, but without a compatible driver the printer still will not work properly.
A secure cable is needed, but Windows still needs the correct driver to use the printer.
The paper size setting affects output but is not needed for the printer to work.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 4
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: Which of the following steps is required to set up print sharing and enable multiple computers to use a shared printer? (Select all that apply)
options: Connect the printer to a computer acting as the print server
Install the necessary printer drivers on each computer
Enable printer sharing in the printer’s properties on the print server computer
Access the network settings on client computers and select the shared printer
Test the print-sharing functionality by sending a print job from a client computer
explanation: To share a printer, connect it to the computer acting as print server and enable sharing in the printer properties on that computer. Install the drivers on each client, connect each client to the shared printer, and send a test print from a client to verify the setup.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 7
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: When would you typically use Printer Control Language (PCL) in printing?
options: Printing documents with complex graphics and images
Printing text-based documents without complex formatting
Printing documents with advanced font rendering and color management
explanation: Printer Control Language (PCL) is a printer language that is efficient for text-based documents without complex formatting, such as ordinary office documents. PostScript is the better choice for complex graphics and precise layouts.
whyWrong: Complex graphics and images are better handled by PostScript.
High-resolution photographs are better handled by PostScript or photo printer technologies.
Advanced font rendering and color management are strengths of PostScript.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 8
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: When unboxing a new print device, which of the following actions should you perform? (Choose three)
options: Remove all protective tapes and packaging materials
A print device should normally be left to acclimate after removing the packaging materials
Install the necessary software and drivers
Load paper and adjust paper settings
Use a two-person lift technique for the printer
Perform a test print to ensure functionality
explanation: Remove all protective tapes and packing materials so that nothing blocks or damages the device. Leave a device that was moved from a cold place to acclimate for a few hours before power on, to avoid condensation. Print devices are heavy, so use a safe two-person lift.
whyWrong: Drivers are installed during setup after the device is unboxed and placed, not during unboxing.
Loading paper is part of setup after unboxing, not an unboxing action.
A test print is done after the device is set up and connected.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 9
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: How does Wi-Fi direct printing work?
options: The printer connects directly to a Wi-Fi network for wireless printing
The printer creates its own Wi-Fi network for devices to connect and print wirelessly
The printer requires a physical connection to a device for wireless printing
The printer uses Bluetooth technology for wireless printing
explanation: With Wi-Fi Direct, the printer creates its own Wi-Fi network and acts like an access point. Devices connect to that network and print without a Wi-Fi router.
whyWrong: Connecting to an existing Wi-Fi network is ordinary wireless printing, not Wi-Fi Direct.
Wi-Fi Direct is wireless and does not need a cable.
Bluetooth is a separate wireless technology from Wi-Fi Direct.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 12
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: How can a duplex printer help reduce excessive paper usage?
options: It automatically prints on both sides of the paper
It prints at a slower speed, conserving paper
It uses recycled paper for printing
It has a larger paper tray, reducing the need for frequent refills
explanation: Duplex printing prints on both sides of the paper automatically, which halves the number of sheets for long documents. Duplex is set in the printer configuration settings.
whyWrong: Printing speed does not change how many sheets a job uses.
Recycled paper is better for the environment but does not reduce the number of sheets.
A larger tray means fewer refills, not less paper used.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 1
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.7 configuration settings (duplex).

stem: What could be the potential cause of a new printer with a duplex unit only being able to print on one side at a time?
options: The printer’s firmware requires an update
The printer’s duplex unit is not properly set up
The printer’s paper tray is not properly aligned
The printer’s ink cartridges are low on ink
explanation: On a new printer, the duplex unit must be installed and set up as the manufacturer’s instructions describe, and duplex must be turned on in the printer settings. Until then, the printer prints on one side only.
whyWrong: A firmware update is unlikely to fix a duplex unit that has not been set up.
The alignment of the paper tray does not control double-sided printing.
Low ink affects print quality, not the ability to print on both sides.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 3
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.7 configuration settings (duplex).

stem: To minimize paper waste and enhance print job control, what measures can be implemented?
options: Load a large stack of paper into the tray
Require a login for print jobs
Avoid using paper trays and feed paper manually
explanation: Requiring a login for print jobs (user authentication with secured prints) means that users must authenticate before their jobs print. This reduces abandoned or unnecessary printouts and gives better control over printing.
whyWrong: A large stack of paper in the tray does not control print jobs or reduce waste.
Double-sided printing reduces paper use but gives no control over who prints what.
Feeding paper manually is impractical for larger jobs and gives no print job control.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 7
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.7 security (user authentication, secured prints).

stem: In a digitization project, which of the following devices would be BEST for capturing electronic images of a large collection of historical handwritten documents?
explanation: Flatbed scanners capture documents accurately without feeding them through rollers, which suits fragile historical handwritten pages. They are commonly used to digitize large numbers of documents.
whyWrong: NFC devices exchange data over a few centimeters, for example for card payments; they cannot capture images.
A digital camera can capture images, but it is less efficient and consistent than a flatbed scanner for a large collection.
A QR scanner reads QR codes, not full document pages.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 19
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.7 ADF/flatbed scanner.

stem: What is the main advantage of using PostScript printing?
explanation: PostScript is a page description language that describes each page in a device-independent way, with advanced graphics capabilities and color management. It gives precise control over graphics and color reproduction, so printed colors are more accurate and consistent. This is why it is popular for graphic design and publishing.
whyWrong: Printing speed depends mostly on the printer's hardware, not on PostScript.
Print resolution is set by the printer's hardware and the source image quality.
Printer security features are not part of the PostScript language.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 11
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101). PostScript's main strength is precise, device-independent rendering of graphics and fonts; color accuracy is the best of the options given.

stem: What is the primary benefit of duplexing in printing?
explanation: Duplexing is printing on both sides of a sheet of paper. It greatly reduces paper use and waste.
whyWrong: Duplex printing does not make printing faster; it is often a little slower because the page must be turned.
Print quality depends on factors such as resolution and the ink or toner, not on duplexing.
Duplexing does not make the printer more durable.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 12
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is an important consideration when properly unboxing a device?
options: Keeping the original packaging materials for future use
Removing all protective films and covers before powering on
Disregarding the instruction manual as it is not necessary
Plugging in the device immediately without inspecting for damage
explanation: When you unbox a device, remove all protective films, covers, packing tape, and shipping restraints before you power it on. Leftover packing material can stop the device from working properly or damage it.
whyWrong: Keeping the original packaging can be useful for a return, but it is not needed to set up the device properly.
The instruction manual has important setup and operation information, so you should not ignore it.
You should inspect the device for damage before you plug it in, not plug it in at once.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 13
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What does adjusting the printer tray settings refer to?
options: Changing the color settings for printed documents
Configuring the network connectivity of the printer
Adjusting the paper size and type for printing
Aligning the print heads for better print quality
explanation: Printer tray settings set the paper size and type (and sometimes the orientation) for each tray. This makes sure that the printer feeds the correct paper from the correct tray for each job.
whyWrong: Color settings control how color is printed, not which paper the trays hold.
Network connectivity is configured in the printer's network settings, not the tray settings.
Printhead alignment is an inkjet maintenance task, not a tray setting.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 14
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is an important consideration when selecting printer paper for optimal print quality?
explanation: When you select printer paper, check that its weight and thickness are compatible with the printer. Paper of the correct weight gives good print quality and prevents paper jams.
whyWrong: Paper color and texture are mostly a matter of preference, not printer compatibility.
The brand or manufacturer matters less than whether the paper weight and thickness meet the printer's requirements.
Price does not decide print quality or whether the paper suits the printer.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 15
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What consumable in laser printers actually makes the text and graphics on the paper?
explanation: Toner is a mix of plastic, silica, and organic compounds. During the fusing step it melts onto the paper and forms the text and graphics.
whyWrong: Ink is the consumable of inkjet printers, not laser printers.
Thermal paper is heat-sensitive paper used by thermal printers.
A ribbon holds the ink that an impact printer strikes onto the paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance, Cram Quiz question 1

stem: What types of printers should include calibration as a maintenance step? (Select all that apply.)
explanation: Both laser and inkjet printers should be calibrated after consumables are replaced. Calibration makes sure the alignment on the X and Y axes is correct.
whyWrong: Thermal printer maintenance is replacing paper, cleaning the heating element, and removing debris, with no calibration step.
Impact printer maintenance is replacing the ribbon, printhead, and paper, with no calibration step.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance, Cram Quiz question 2

stem: What type of printer uses special heat-sensitive paper in lieu of traditional ink?
explanation: Thermal printers use a thermal head that heats up and forms text on special heat-sensitive paper. They need no ink, toner, or ribbon.
whyWrong: Laser printers fuse toner onto regular paper.
Inkjet printers spray ink onto regular paper.
Impact printers strike an inked ribbon onto continuous-feed or multipart paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance, Cram Quiz question 3

stem: What type of printer can use multipart paper?
explanation: Multipart paper makes several copies of a document at the same time. Impact printers strike the paper with pins through an inked ribbon, and that force activates the carbon or carbonless layers of multipart paper.
whyWrong: Laser printers put no physical force on the paper, so they cannot make copies on multipart paper.
Inkjet printers spray ink without striking the paper, so the lower layers of multipart paper get no copy.
Thermal printers only heat special paper and do not press hard enough to mark multipart paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You are preparing to perform laser printer maintenance. Which of the following should you consider?
options: Replace toner, apply maintenance kit, calibrate, and clean.
Replace paper, clean heating element, and remove debris.
Replace ribbon, replace print head, and replace paper.
Clean printheads, replace cartridges, calibrate, and clear jams.
explanation: Laser printer maintenance includes replacing toner, applying a maintenance kit, calibrating, and cleaning. The maintenance kit replaces worn parts such as the fuser and rollers at the page count the manufacturer gives.
whyWrong: Replacing paper, cleaning the heating element, and removing debris is thermal printer maintenance.
Replacing the ribbon, printhead, and paper is impact printer maintenance.
Cleaning printheads, replacing cartridges, calibrating, and clearing jams is inkjet printer maintenance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 20: Printer Maintenance, Cram Quiz question 5

stem: A user informs you that color printouts are noticeably different from what appears on their screen (incorrect chroma display). What actions should you take? (Select two.)
options: Ensure that ink/toner cartridges aren’t empty.
Make sure the separation pad is getting enough traction.
Ensure that the paper is not too thin.
explanation: A printout always differs slightly from the screen, but a very noticeable difference means you should check that no ink or toner color is empty. Then run the printer's calibration tool to adjust the color output as necessary.
whyWrong: Separation pad traction affects multipage misfeeds, not color.
Paper that is too thin causes misfeeds or jams, not wrong colors.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 2
note: Incorrect chroma display was a printer symptom in the older objectives; the current 5.6 list has no color symptom, so the question is tagged to printer calibration in 3.8.

stem: Which of the following are usually included in a laser printer maintenance kit? (Select the two best answers.)
explanation: Laser printer maintenance kits usually include paper pickup rollers, transfer rollers, and a fuser. Toner cartridges are not included in maintenance kits.
whyWrong: The image drum is usually part of the toner cartridge, not the maintenance kit.
Toner comes in separate toner cartridges, not in maintenance kits.
The duplexer is a part of the printer for two-sided printing, not a maintenance kit item.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 4

stem: You have been called to a customer site to perform maintenance on an impact printer. Which should you consider?
options: Replacing paper, cleaning heating element, and removing debris
Replacing toner, applying maintenance kit, calibrating, and cleaning
Replacing ribbon, replacing print head, and replacing paper
Cleaning heads, replacing cartridges, calibrating, and clearing jams
explanation: Impact printer maintenance includes replacing the ribbon, replacing the print head, and replacing paper. Each printer type has its own maintenance tasks, so match the procedure to the technology.
whyWrong: Replacing paper, cleaning the heating element, and removing debris is thermal printer maintenance.
Replacing toner, applying a maintenance kit, calibrating, and cleaning is laser printer maintenance.
Cleaning heads, replacing cartridges, calibrating, and clearing jams is inkjet printer maintenance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 28: Troubleshooting Printers, Cram Quiz question 7

stem: Which of the following should be reset during normal printer maintenance?
explanation: Reset the page count whenever you perform normal, scheduled printer maintenance. A laser printer, for example, may print about 200,000 pages before it needs a maintenance kit, so the reset counter shows when the next maintenance is due.
whyWrong: The job queue resets on its own when the printer is turned off for maintenance.
The print job cache clears on its own when the printer is turned off for maintenance.
Tray settings do not need to be reset during maintenance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 5

stem: Which of the following types of printers requires a maintenance kit that contains a fuser, a transfer roller, and pickup rollers?
explanation: The laser printer is the type most associated with maintenance kits. A common laser printer maintenance kit includes a fuser assembly, a transfer roller, and pickup rollers.
whyWrong: A thermal printer's main parts are the feed assembly and the heating element, and it has no fuser.
An inkjet printer uses ink cartridges and a print head, not a fuser or a transfer roller.
An impact printer uses a print head, a ribbon, and a tractor feed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 30

stem: Which of the following printer technologies uses piezoelectric pressure pads to produce small bubbles that are moved to the paper?
explanation: Inkjet printers force tiny droplets of ink from the printhead onto the paper. Piezoelectric inkjets flex a crystal to push each droplet out, and thermal inkjets heat the ink to form a bubble that does the same.
whyWrong: A laser printer applies toner to the paper in an electrophotographic imaging process.
A thermal printer heats specially coated thermal paper to create text and images.
An impact printer hammers characters through an inked ribbon onto the paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 40
note: Book explanation reworded: piezoelectric inkjets push droplets out by flexing a crystal; the bubble method belongs to thermal inkjets.

stem: A user with an inkjet printer states that all color printouts are missing red ink. The printer has cartridges for each of the CMYK colors, and the user has recently replaced the magenta cartridge. Which of the following steps should be performed NEXT?
options: Verify that the printer cables are connected.
Use paper of a different weight.
explanation: Clean the printhead, because a clogged printhead can stop one color from printing even when the cartridge is new. Most printers include an onscreen utility for this, or you can clean the printhead manually and gently. If colors are only slightly off, calibrate the printer.
whyWrong: Disconnected cables would stop all printing, not one color.
Maintenance kits are mostly used for laser printers and are not needed here.
The weight of the paper does not affect which colors an inkjet printer prints.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – A+ Core 1 (220-1201) Practice Exam, Practice Exam question 51

stem: Which types of printers are referred to as page printers because they receive their print job instructions one page at a time? (Choose two.)
explanation: A page printer is a type of computer printer that prints a page at a time. Common types of page printers are the inkjet printer and the laser printer.
whyWrong: Impact printers such as dot-matrix printers print one line at a time, not a page at a time.
Thermal printers, such as receipt printers, are not called page printers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 2

stem: You have a finance manager who needs to print contracts in triplicate. Which type of printers are BEST for printing on multipart forms?
explanation: Dot-matrix printers are impact printers and therefore are the best for multipart forms. The pins strike the ribbon hard enough to print through every copy of the form.
whyWrong: Inkjet printers spray ink and do not strike the paper, so they cannot print on the carbon copies.
Laser printers do not strike the paper, so they cannot print on multipart forms.
Thermal printers use heat on special paper and cannot print on multipart forms.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 4

stem: Which step in the EP imaging process uses a laser to discharge selected areas of the photosensitive drum, thus forming an image on the drum?
explanation: The exposing step uses a laser to discharge selected areas of the photosensitive drum, thus forming an image on the drum. This happens after charging and before developing.
whyWrong: The transferring step moves the toner from the drum to the paper.
The developing step puts toner on the exposed areas of the drum.
The cleaning step removes leftover toner and charge from the drum.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 5
note: The EP imaging process is not named in 220-1201 3.8; tagged with the closest topic, laser printers.

stem: Which device in an inkjet printer contains the printhead?
explanation: In an inkjet printer, the ink cartridge is the actual printhead. This is where the ink is expelled to form letters or graphics.
whyWrong: Toner cartridges are used by laser printers to store toner.
A daisy wheel is the part that strikes the letters onto the paper in a daisy-wheel printer.
Paper trays are storage bins from which the pickup rollers feed paper into the printer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 8

stem: What is the correct order of the steps in the EP imaging process?
options: Developing, exposing, transferring, fusing, charging, cleaning, processing
Charging, processing, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning
Processing, transferring, exposing, developing, charging, cleaning, fusing
Processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, cleaning
explanation: The correct sequence in the EP imaging process is processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning. The drum must be charged before the laser can expose the image, and toner must be developed onto the drum before it can be transferred to the paper.
whyWrong: The process cannot start with developing, because the drum has not yet been charged or exposed.
Processing must come before charging, because the printer processes the page image first.
Transferring cannot come before exposing and developing, because there is no toner image yet.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 9
note: The EP imaging process is not named in 220-1201 3.8; tagged with the closest topic, laser printers.

stem: What is typically included in the EP laser printer toner cartridge? (Choose three.)
explanation: An electrophotographic (EP) laser printer toner cartridge includes the toner, print drum, and cleaning blade. The laser is usually contained within the printer, not within the toner cartridge.
whyWrong: The laser is part of the printer itself, not the toner cartridge.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 11

stem: What happens during the developing stage of laser printing?
options: An electrostatic charge is applied to the drum to attract toner particles.
Heat is applied to the paper to melt the toner.
The laser creates an image of the page on the drum.
An electrostatic charge is applied to the paper to attract toner particles.
explanation: After a laser has created an image of the page, the developing roller uses a magnet and electrostatic charges to attract toner to itself. It then transfers the toner to the areas on the drum that have been exposed to the laser.
whyWrong: Heat melts the toner into the paper during the fusing stage.
The laser creates the image of the page on the drum during the exposing stage.
A charge is applied to the paper during the transferring stage, which comes right after developing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 12
note: The EP imaging process is not named in 220-1201 3.8; tagged with the closest topic, laser printers.

stem: Which printer contains a wheel that looks like a flower with raised letters and symbols on each “petal”?
explanation: The daisy-wheel printer gets its name because it contains a wheel with raised letters and symbols on each “petal.” It is an impact printer that strikes the character through a ribbon onto the paper.
whyWrong: Inkjet printers spray ink through nozzles and have no character wheel.
Dot-matrix printers form characters from a grid of pins, not from a wheel of letters.
Laser printers form the image on a drum with a laser and toner.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 15
note: Daisy-wheel printers are obsolete; tagged with the closest topic, impact printers.

stem: What part of a laser printer supplies the voltages for charging and transferring corona assemblies?
explanation: The high-voltage power supply (HVPS) is the part of the laser printer that supplies the voltages for the charging and transferring corona assemblies. The DC power supply powers the printer's logic and motors.
whyWrong: The DC power supply provides low DC voltages for the printer's circuits and motors.
The controller circuitry turns the computer's signals into instructions for the printer assemblies.
The transfer corona uses the high voltage; it does not supply it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 16
note: Laser printer internal parts are not named in 220-1201 3.8; tagged with the closest topic, laser printers.

stem: Which printer part gets the toner from the photosensitive drum onto the paper?
explanation: The transfer corona assembly gets the toner from the photosensitive drum onto the paper. For some printers, this is a transfer corona wire; for others, it is a transfer corona roller.
whyWrong: The laser-scanning assembly writes the image onto the drum.
The fusing assembly melts the toner into the paper after it has been transferred.
The drum holds the toner image, but the corona assembly is what pulls the toner onto the paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 17
note: Laser printer internal parts are not named in 220-1201 3.8; tagged with the closest topic, laser printers.

stem: Which step in the laser printer printing process occurs immediately after the exposing phase?
explanation: Developing happens after exposing. The correct order is processing, charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning.
whyWrong: Charging comes before exposing, not after it.
Fusing comes after transferring, near the end of the process.
Transferring comes after developing.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 18
note: The EP imaging process is not named in 220-1201 3.8; tagged with the closest topic, laser printers.

stem: Which laser printer component permanently presses the toner into the paper?
explanation: The fuser assembly presses and melts the toner into the paper. It uses heat and pressure, which is why pages come out of a laser printer warm.
whyWrong: The transfer corona moves the toner from the drum to the paper but does not fix it in place.
The printer controller circuitry converts signals from the PC into signals for the printer assemblies.
The paper transport assembly controls the movement of the paper through the printer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter), Volume 1 – Chapter 5: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Review Questions question 19

stem: What mechanism is used by most inkjet printers to push ink onto the paper?
explanation: Most inkjet printers use heat to move the ink: tiny resistors or electroconductive plates at the end of each tube boil the ink. This makes a tiny air bubble that pushes a droplet of ink onto the paper.
whyWrong: Electrostatic charges are used in laser printers, not to push ink in an inkjet.
Gravity alone cannot place tiny ink droplets on the paper.
Inkjets do not use air pressure to push the ink.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 1
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 26: the current inkjet topic covers parts and maintenance; closest topic.

stem: With a laser printer, what creates the image on the imaging drum?
explanation: The laser imaging unit creates an image on the imaging drum. The laser writes a pattern of reduced charge onto the drum, and toner sticks to those areas.
whyWrong: The primary corona puts a uniform charge on the drum before the image is written.
The transfer corona pulls the toner from the drum onto the paper.
Toner is the powder that forms the printed image, not what writes it on the drum.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 2
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 26: the laser imaging process (220-1101 3.7) is not in the current objectives, which list laser maintenance only; closest topic.

stem: What is the proper order of the laser printing process?
options: Process, clean, charge, expose, develop, transfer, and fuse
Process, charge, expose, develop, transfer, fuse, and clean
Clean, expose, develop, transfer, process, fuse, and charge
Clean, charge, expose, process, develop, fuse, and transfer
explanation: The laser printing process is process, charge, expose, develop, transfer, fuse, and clean. The printer may run the steps in a different order, but this is the usual order.
whyWrong: Cleaning is the last step of the process, not the second.
The process starts with processing the image, not with cleaning.
Fusing comes after transferring the toner to the paper, not before it.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 3
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 26: the laser imaging process (220-1101 3.7) is not in the current objectives, which list laser maintenance only; closest topic.

stem: On a dot-matrix printer, what physically strikes the ribbon to form an image?
explanation: Printwires physically strike the ribbon in dot-matrix printers. The printhead fires its pins against the ribbon to form each character from dots.
whyWrong: Electromagnets drive the printwires but do not strike the ribbon themselves.
A character wheel is used by daisy-wheel printers, not dot-matrix printers.
Print hammers are used in line printers, not dot-matrix printheads.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 4

stem: Which of these items are considered to be dot-matrix printer consumables? (Select two.)
explanation: Both paper and ribbons are dot-matrix printer consumables. They are used up and must be replaced regularly.
whyWrong: A drive motor is a mechanical part that lasts for the life of the printer.
A flywheel is a mechanical part, not something used up during printing.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 5

stem: What part of a laser printer must be vacuumed or replaced periodically to prevent damage caused by the action of the corona?
explanation: The ozone filter of a laser printer should be periodically vacuumed or changed. The corona makes ozone, which can damage printer parts and irritate people.
whyWrong: Rubber rollers wear from moving paper, not from the corona's ozone.
Transfer filter is not a standard laser printer part.
The cleaning blade scrapes leftover toner off the drum and does not handle ozone.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 6

stem: Which printing process ends with the physical and electrical cleaning of the imaging drum?
explanation: The laser printing process ends with the physical and electrical cleaning of the imaging drum. A rubber blade scrapes off leftover toner, and erase lamps remove any remaining charge.
whyWrong: Thermal printers heat special paper and have no imaging drum.
Inkjet printers spray ink and have no imaging drum to clean.
Impact printers strike a ribbon and have no imaging drum.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Chapter 26: Printers and Multifunction Devices, Chapter Review question 9
note: All-in-One 11e (220-1101/1102) Ch. 26: the laser imaging process (220-1101 3.7) is not in the current objectives; closest topic is Laser (clean).

stem: What happens during the charging stage of a laser printer?
options: Toner particles are attracted to the charged areas on the drum
The laser beam scans the photosensitive drum, creating an electrostatic image
Any residual toner or debris is removed from the drum and other components
The primary corona wire charges the photosensitive drum uniformly
explanation: In the charging stage, the primary corona wire or primary charge roller gives the photosensitive drum a uniform negative charge. This prepares the drum for the exposing stage.
whyWrong: Toner is attracted to the drum in the developing stage.
The laser draws the electrostatic image on the drum in the exposing stage.
Leftover toner is removed from the drum in the cleaning stage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 2
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 listed the laser imaging process; 220-1201 3.8 lists only laser maintenance, so this is background for 3.8.

stem: Which type of printer typically uses a laser beam or LED light source for image formation?
explanation: Laser printers use a laser beam, or an LED array in LED printers, to create an electrostatic image on a photosensitive drum. The drum then picks up toner, which is fused onto the paper.
whyWrong: A dot matrix printer forms characters with pins that strike an inked ribbon.
A thermal printer uses heat on special heat-sensitive paper.
An impact printer strikes an inked ribbon against the paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 3
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.6 (printers and MFDs).

stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of a laser printer?
options: Charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning
Cleaning, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and charging
Charging, exposing, developing, fusing, transferring, and cleaning
Cleaning, exposing, developing, transferring, and fusing
explanation: The laser printing process goes charging, exposing, developing, transferring, fusing, and cleaning. The drum is charged, the laser writes the image, toner sticks to the image, the toner moves to the paper, heat and pressure fuse it, and the drum is cleaned for the next page.
whyWrong: Cleaning prepares the drum for the next page after the print; charging must come first in this sequence.
Toner must be transferred to the paper before it can be fused.
This list starts with cleaning and leaves out the charging stage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 8
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 listed the laser imaging process; 220-1201 3.8 lists only laser maintenance, so this is background for 3.8.

stem: Which type of printer generates images by applying heat to special heat-sensitive paper that needs to be kept out of direct sunlight?
explanation: Thermal printers use a heated print head on special heat-sensitive paper, which darkens where it is heated. The paper must be kept out of direct sunlight and heat, which also darken it.
whyWrong: A laser printer uses a laser, a drum, and toner on plain paper.
A dot matrix printer uses pins that strike an inked ribbon.
An impact printer strikes an inked ribbon against plain or multipart paper.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 9
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.6 (printers and MFDs).

stem: What happens during the fusing stage of a laser printer?
options: The toner on the paper is fused and melted into the fibers
Toner particles are attracted to the charged areas on the drum
Any residual toner or debris is removed from the drum and other components
The laser beam scans the photosensitive drum, creating an electrostatic image
explanation: In the fusing stage, the heated fuser rollers apply heat and pressure that melt the toner into the paper fibers. This bonds the toner to the paper permanently.
whyWrong: Toner is attracted to the drum in the developing stage.
Leftover toner is removed from the drum in the cleaning stage.
The laser draws the electrostatic image on the drum in the exposing stage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.6 question 11
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 listed the laser imaging process; 220-1201 3.8 lists only laser maintenance, so this is background for 3.8.

stem: Which component is responsible for the charging stage in a laser printer?
explanation: The primary corona wire, a thin wire close to the photosensitive drum, does the charging stage in a laser printer. It gives the drum a uniform charge for the next stages; newer printers use a primary charge roller instead.
whyWrong: The toner cartridge supplies toner for the developing stage.
The drum receives the charge; it does not create it.
The fuser assembly melts the toner onto the paper in the fusing stage.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 1
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 listed the laser imaging process; 220-1201 3.8 lists only laser maintenance, so this is background for 3.8.

stem: What components are typically included in a printer maintenance kit?
options: New fuser assembly, transfer/secondary charge roller, and paper transport rollers
New toner cartridges and cleaning sheets
Additional paper trays and feeder units
explanation: A laser printer maintenance kit usually contains a new fuser assembly, which is the main part of the kit. It also has a transfer/secondary charge roller and paper transport rollers, such as pickup rollers and separation pads.
whyWrong: Toner cartridges are replaced separately as supplies, not in the maintenance kit.
Ink cartridges and printheads are inkjet parts, not laser maintenance kit parts.
Paper trays and feeder units are optional accessories, not maintenance parts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 3: Hardware, Objective 3.7 question 13
note: Old objective 220-1101 3.7 (printer maintenance).

stem: What could be the potential cause of printed text not sticking to the paper?
options: The printer is using low-quality ink cartridges
The paper being used is not compatible with the printer
The printer’s fuser unit is not functioning properly
The printer’s temperature settings are too low
explanation: The fuser unit in a laser printer uses heat and pressure to melt the toner onto the paper. If the fuser is not working properly, the printed text does not stick and smears or rubs off.
whyWrong: Ink cartridges are not used in laser printers, and poor ink affects quality, not whether toner sticks.
Unsuitable paper can affect print quality, but loose toner that rubs off points to the fuser.
The fuser temperature is controlled by the printer itself, not by a user setting.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 2
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.8 laser printer maintenance (fuser in the maintenance kit).

stem: Why is a printer printing blank receipts?
options: Paper feed issues or incorrect paper loading
explanation: Receipt printers are thermal printers, which print on special heat-sensitive paper. Blank receipts are usually caused by incorrect paper loading (the paper inserted the wrong way round) or by paper feed problems.
whyWrong: Thermal receipt printers use heat-sensitive paper and have no ink or toner cartridges.
An overheated print head darkens the paper; it does not leave receipts blank.
An outdated driver can cause print errors, but it is not the usual cause of blank receipts.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 10
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.8 thermal printers (special thermal paper, feed assembly).

stem: What type of printer typically uses a ribbon?
explanation: A dot matrix printer is an impact printer: its print head pins strike an ink-soaked ribbon against the paper to form characters. The ribbon is replaced as part of its maintenance.
whyWrong: Inkjet printers use liquid ink cartridges or tanks, not ribbons.
Laser printers use toner cartridges with powdered toner, not ribbons.
Direct thermal printers use heat-sensitive paper and do not need a ribbon.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 11
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.8 impact printers.

stem: Why does a dot matrix printer produce documents with missing words?
explanation: When a dot matrix printer ribbon becomes worn, it no longer transfers ink properly to parts of the paper, which leaves gaps and missing words. Replace the ribbon.
whyWrong: Paper feed problems or misalignment give skewed prints or jams, not missing words.
Overheating affects the overall print quality rather than leaving out words.
An outdated driver can cause print errors, but it is not the usual cause of missing words.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 5: Hardware and Network Troubleshooting, Objective 5.6 question 12
note: Old 220-1101 objective 5.6 (printers). Tagged to current 3.8 impact printer maintenance (replace ribbon).

stem: What does inkjet calibration involve?
options: Adjusting the ink cartridge settings for optimal performance
Aligning the print heads to ensure precise ink placement
Changing the inkjet printer’s connection settings
Cleaning the inkjet carriage to remove debris and dust
explanation: Inkjet calibration aligns the printheads so that ink is placed precisely on the paper. This improves print quality, especially for fine details and images.
whyWrong: Ink cartridge settings involve monitoring ink levels and replacing cartridges, not calibration.
Connection settings control how the printer connects to computers, not calibration.
Cleaning the carriage is a separate maintenance task from calibration.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 16
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: What is the function of an inkjet carriage belt in a printer?
options: Transferring ink from the cartridge to the printhead
Controlling the movement of the printhead assembly
Ensuring proper paper feed and alignment
Maintaining optimal ink flow and print quality
explanation: The inkjet carriage belt moves the printhead assembly back and forth across the paper. It is attached to the printhead carriage and positions the printhead precisely so that ink droplets land in the correct place.
whyWrong: The ink supply system moves ink from the cartridge to the printhead, not the belt.
Paper feed and alignment are controlled by the feed rollers and paper guides.
Ink flow and print quality depend on the ink, printhead maintenance, and calibration, not directly on the belt.
source: CompTIA A+ Practice Tests Core 1 (220-1101) and Core 2 (220-1102) (Neil) – Chapter 6: Mock Exam: Core 1 (220-1101), Mock Exam question 17
note: Neil Core 1 mock exam (220-1101).

stem: A user needs to connect a laptop that has only a DisplayPort output to a projector that has only an HDMI input. What is the BEST solution?
options: A new projector with a VGA port
explanation: When the devices or cables do not match, an adapter makes the connection. A DisplayPort-to-HDMI adapter lets the laptop's DisplayPort output drive the projector's HDMI input.
whyWrong: A USB-to-RJ-45 adapter adds a wired network port, not a video connection.
Buying a new projector is costly and VGA would not match the laptop's DisplayPort output either.
A longer HDMI cable still cannot plug into the laptop's DisplayPort output.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 13: Cables and Connectors

stem: What does the 80 Plus certification of a power supply mean?
options: It converts at least 80 percent of the AC power it draws into DC power
It supplies at least 80 watts on the 12 V rail
It runs on 80 to 240 VAC input
It can supply 80 percent of its rating for a short time after a power failure
explanation: A power supply converts AC power to DC power, and some power is always lost as heat. An 80 Plus power supply converts 80 percent or more of the power it draws into DC power; higher levels (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Titanium) are more efficient.
whyWrong: 80 Plus is an efficiency rating, not a minimum wattage on one rail.
The input voltage range is a separate rating from 80 Plus efficiency.
A power supply has no stored power after a failure; that is the job of a UPS.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power

stem: A company wants new workstation power supplies that waste as little power as possible as heat. Which certification level is the BEST choice?
explanation: The 80 Plus certification has several efficiency levels. Titanium is the highest level, so it converts the most AC power into DC power and loses the least as heat.
whyWrong: Bronze is one of the lower 80 Plus levels, so more power is lost as heat.
The standard 80 Plus level is the least efficient certified level.
Silver is more efficient than Bronze but less efficient than Gold, Platinum, and Titanium.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 18: Power
